📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Inbetweeners at Newcastle United, can they become success stories this series (this season) and beyond.

So much could depend on how this quarter perform.

Just in case you weren’t aware, The Inbetweeners is a brilliant (in my opinion anyway) comedy series (that has also then produced a couple of excellent films).

This comedy is the story of four teenagers who are misfits, neither totally cool nor total outcasts (hence The Inbetweeners), who regularly find themselves in awkward situations of their own making,.

This fictional quartet occasionally hint of moving on to a consistently successful level, but their own inherent frailties as well as outside factors, time after time conspire to prevent those glimpses of promise becoming ever more than that.

My focus isn’t on individuals who have just arrived this summer at St James’ Park, it isn’t on young players, it isn’t on older players where we pretty much know what we are going to get.

When it comes to The Inbetweeners at Newcastle United, I wanted to concentrate on this quartet below.

Four players who have played plenty of Premier League football in their careers and have shown enough to suggest they COULD be notable, indeed vital, for Newcastle United this season.

All four of them also happen to play in the key midfield and attacking positions, the positions where United need far higher input and productivity if they are to create the chances and score the goals that can make the (positive) difference this season.

So without further ado, here are The Inbetweeners at St James’ Park:.

I think that arguably he is THE ultimate Inbetweener at Newcastle United. He was brilliant in that 2022-23 fourth place finish season before then serious injury hit then fitness and form challenges have followed.

At times we see THAT Joe Willock of 2022-23 and the second half on Saturday a prime example. Against his former club he was the key man in that second half,  the pressing of opposition players and his running with the ball, the Arsenal midfield couldn’t handle him at times. Willock pressured Odegaard into the mistake that produced the equaliser and then an assist for Thiaw’s strike.

Joe Willock would deserve to be first name on the team sheet if he consistently played like he did in that second half.

Started the season in electric form, confidence sky high as he scored within five minutes of the opening game against Liverpool, then in the first EPL away game scored a brilliant goal to set United on their way to beating Spurs.

Then injury hit and when he has returned, it feels a bit like Snakes and Ladders. He climbed plenty of ladders and got into a great position brimming with confidence, he then though hits one snake that sends his confidence and form sliding right back to rock bottom and needing to start again.

I bit like Willock and Saturday’s second half, Elanga needs to simply get his head back in the place it was when Liverpool and Spurs couldn’t handle him. He is capable of being a huge player for Matthias Jaissle AND he needs to be that player to solve our problem on the right. He did alright on Saturday when he came on and maybe a huge factor can be if Tino Livramento now can stay fit as well on that side.

Very similar story to Anthony Elanga, started this season on fire and then lost his way.

It has been revealed that in certain moments, Yoane Wissa has looked unplayable (in a good way!) this season, some of his runs on the ball have been exhilarating. The one he made with a handful of Liverpool players challenging him half the length of the pitch before passing to Joe Willock for his goal, where has that gone?

Again like Elanga, with Wissa it feels like it is very much a confidence thing.

Sources indicate that he had an astonishing record at Brentford but I do feel he is an attacker who is more of a team player, he needs those around him also playing well. Hopefully if the team overall can become more consistent and then Yoane Wissa finds within that some special moments of his own, we can just maybe have that opening of this season player back again.

Of this quartet of Inbetweeners at Newcastle United, I think Ramsey deserves to be cut the most slack.

The former Villa star has still only started 15 Premier League matches for Newcastle United and was very unlucky with a bad early injury last season (thanks to Sean Longstaff) and desperately needs a run in the team to get his rhythm after having his own struggles with fitness and form.

Like the other three above, Jacob Ramsey has had moments where we can see the player Eddie Howe signed. The same as Joe Willock, Ramsey is very mobile, runs well with the ball, can be very effective with a high press, can be a difference maker.

According to recent reports, the second half on Saturday he showed that and I do think that if Newcastle United are to exceed any current expectations, we need to have players with pace who can quickly carry the ball in transition an cause problems for opposition teams on a regular basis. If Jacob Ramsey and Joe Willock can do it against the best team in the country, admittedly just for one half on Saturday, why can’t they do it against the rest?

Once again though, the same as Yoane Wissa and Anthony Elanga, it is all about this quarter losing their status as The Inbetweeners at Newcastle United and proving to be something far better than that.

Here’s hoping they prove they are worthy of another series.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Back in July, Kyle Healy-Matthews was tempted away from West Ham by Newcastle United.

The highly teenage starlet was a young player the Hammers were desperate not to lose.

Newcastle United fighting off a number of other Premier League clubs who had been competing to attract the teenage right-back.

However, personal terms were agreed between NUFC and Kyle Healy-Matthews and the deal completed.

Obviously one for the future he looked a very positive addition, the young right-back is quick and with very good defensive ability, he’d been a stand out player in the West Ham young set-up.

Since the October 2021 takeover, Newcastle United having signed a lot of promising young players from other clubs, which will hopefully pay longer-term benefits.

Now Newcastle United have revealed on Wednesday morning that Kyle Healy-Matthews has signed his first professional contract with the club on his 17th birthday.

Sources indicate that official Newcastle United media stating: ‘The Romford-born youngster joined Newcastle’s Academy from West Ham United last summer and initially linked up with Chris Moore’s Under-18s squad as a first-year scholar before agreeing professional terms with the Magpies. Healy-Matthews, who primarily plays as a right-back, expressed his delight in committing his future with Newcastle and has relished his time at United’s Little Benton Academy to date.’.

Kyle Healy-Matthews: “I’m very pleased to sign my first professional contract,” he told newcastleunited.com. “It’s a special moment for myself and my family, seeing all the hard work which has led up to this. Newcastle is a massive club with goals and ambitions that I feel I can contribute in. I believe I can play a big part for this club. I’ve enjoyed my time here a lot. I’ve had a lot of support from my peers and coaches with helping me to settle in as well as progressing along the way.”.

The official NUFC media going on to say: ‘Kyle Healy-Matthews, who cites fellow right-back Kyle Walker as his footballing idol, has made a positive start to the current campaign at Under-18 level, with the Toon teenagers winning six of their opening seven league matches and currently occupying third spot in the division. The rapid full-back believes he has handled the challenge of relocating hundreds of miles away from home for the first time and is determined to advance through the Magpies’ youth ranks. Healy-Matthews, a member of West Ham’s Under-17 Premier League Cup winning side last season.’.

According to recent reports, kyle Healy-Matthews: “I’ve only been here for a few months but I think I can say the move has paid off. Moving very far away from home could have been tricky but with all of the support I had around me from my peers, that really helped me to settle in swiftly. I’m loving my time with the Under-18s. This season, my main aim is to progress into the Under-21s and long-term, but hopefully not too long, would be to progress into the first-team.”.

Steve Harper is Newcastle United Academy Director: “Kyle has made an excellent impression since joining the Academy in the summer and we’re pleased to see him rewarded with his first professional contract. Moving away from home and settling into a upcoming environment can be a significant challenge for any young player but Kyle has handled the transition brilliantly. He’s worked extremely hard since arriving at the club and his attitude, commitment and willingness to learn have stood out throughout his time here so far. This contract is recognition of the progress he’s made, and we’re excited to continue supporting his development as he takes the next steps in his career at Newcastle United.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to reports from Italy, Liverpool are regularly scouting a red-hot striker who’s emerged as a shock candidate for the Golden Boot in Serie A this season.

Andoni Iraola has been almost exclusively reliant on Alexander Isak at centre-forward since taking charge of the Reds in the summer, with Hugo Ekitike continuing his recovery from a long-term Achilles injury.

The Frenchman is targeting a return to action next month (The Athletic), although it appears that Anfield chiefs are keeping tabs on a positional alternative who’s emerging as a breakthrough sensation in one of Europe’s major leagues.

A report from Corriere dello Sport has claimed that Liverpool are sending scouts ‘every week’ to watch Gustavo Varela, who’s been in remarkable goalscoring form with Monza since joining the Serie A outfit in the summer.

Napoli and Juventus have also been strongly linked with the 21-year-old, who’s been the subject of enquiries from Tottenham, Brentford and Sunderland, with the list of suitors growing in tandem with his goal return in the Italian top flight.

Ivan Juric’s side reportedly want €40m (£33.5m) for the Portuguese hitman, which’d represent a monumental profit on a player they signed from Gil Vicente in July for a paltry €2.5m (£2.1m).

(Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images).

Recent findings suggest that want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

Varela is at the moment the leading scorer in Serie A this season with nine goals, which is remarkable when his team are currently in the relegation zone, and he accounts for more than half of their goal tally in the top flight so far.

For someone who’d scored just seven times in 34 senior appearances before the summer, his form since joining Monza has been extraordinary. Should that continue, it’s safe to say that he won’t be at the Stadio Brianteo for much longer.

What Liverpool would need to consider is whether this is a mere purple patch from the Portuguese youngster, or the start of a journey towards being one of Europe’s most feared centre-forwards.

Varela has scored nine Serie A goals from an xG of just 5.48 (Fotmob), an astonishing overperformance which begs the question as to whether he can maintain that for a full campaign.

If Isak keeps up his own hot streak and Ekitike gets back to the levels he’d shown prior to his injury, it’d be difficult to see the Monza striker getting much of a look-in at Anfield.

However, it’s easy to see why Liverpool are routinely dispatching scouts to gather information on one of the breakout stars of European football in 2026.

West Ham’s manager Scott Parker, from his demeanour last night, is understandably in a pretty dark place just now after losing his second game in charge, four games now without a win: West Ham now twelfth in the second division with two points from their last eighteen.

Relegation, not promotion form.

“If you are going through hell, keep going” is the oft-quoted popular saying, accredited to Winston Churchill but applicable to just about any circumstance when deep in the smelly stuff.

It’s only football. We understand. But it is supposed to be the very salvation from all of the bad things going on in the world right now.

Which is why it feels pretty lousy being a West Ham fan right now, especially those intrepid away fans who braved the worst of the British transport system and weather to turn up and support their team at Fratton Park.

“The day is darkest just before the dawn” – It was pretty damn’ dark at Fratton Park last night.

How long must that journey home have felt, arriving home in the wee small hours replaying a kind of mental lowlights reel – and there were a few lowlights, let’s face it.

Most worrying of all is that the Championship’s top scorers seemingly now cannot put the ball in the back of the net.

Industry observers note that however, a sneaky peek at the ‘bookies latest odds suggest they know something we don’t, with West Ham still odds-on (3/10 this morning) to finish in the top six. I’m not a betting man but strip away the emotion (which this ‘morning after’ column is supposed to do ) and there’s still a cold, calculating expectation that someone – presumably Scott Parker – can turn this ship around. There’s still time.

In a recent development, west Ham are the width of a goal post away from fourth place. The season is long and it is not yet December. Get behind whichever eleven are sent out to do battle with Stoke on Saturday. And wait for the dodgy decision in our favour or the outrageous deflected goal that we don’t deserve – which will signal a change of fortunes. COYI!

💡 Key Takeaways

  • That goal put Newcastle United 2-1 up on 62 minutes.
  • Graham Scott refereed in the Premier League for a decade and he was also a video assistant referee (VAR) more than 100 times.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Graham Scott has been quizzed by an Arsenal fan as to why Malick Thiaw’s goal was allowed to stand on Saturday.

That goal put Newcastle United 2-1 up on 62 minutes.

Graham Scott refereed in the Premier League for a decade and he was also a video assistant referee (VAR) more than 100 times.

Now retired, he brings his unique insight into how match officials operate for The Athletic.

They invite readers to send in questions each week for Graham Scott to answer.

This week the former top referee received this one from an Arsenal fan….

‘Why did neither the referee nor VAR penalise the holding on Jurrien Timber that allowed Dan Burn to win a free header to create Newcastle’s second goal against Arsenal?’.

Graham Scott explaining: “Timber was impeded by Will Osula as he chased after Burn (circled below). Osula was impeded by Declan Rice, who was holding him with both arms. Malick Thiaw was being held by Martin Odegaard, who was being held by Thiaw. Lewis Miley blocked Ezri Konsa, who pulled Miley to get past him. There were probably other potential fouls, too. The officials look for the most serious offences that have the greatest impact, and none of these came close to meeting those thresholds — which are set by the league and the lawmakers, not the refs.”.

I know that no football fan takes it well when any decision goes against them BUT as a group I think Arsenal fans do appear especially bizarre in terms of not willing to accept any decision that doesn’t go their way.

Graham Scott was also asked another question regarding Saturday’s game….

Industry observers note that ‘When David Raya went down for treatment the first time at Newcastle on Saturday, why did another Arsenal player not have to leave the field for a minute? I thought that was the new rule.’.

It has been revealed that graham Scott: ‘No Arsenal player was asked to leave the field for a minute because Raya had collided with an opponent and requested treatment at the earliest opportunity. There is a similar exemption if a goalkeeper’s injury occurs from a foul that the referee deems worthy of a yellow or red card. This rule was introduced to stop goalkeepers mysteriously sitting down and demanding treatment for fictitious muscle injuries while their coach held an impromptu time-out chat with the rest of the team.’.

I have to confess, I totally forgot about this new rule coming in. Has any goalkeeper got ‘injured’ this season and had treatment on the pitch which led to his Premier League side going down to ten men for a minute with an outfield player going off?

#119029. Aberdeen boss Mario Frick's heavy metal football is music to the ears of their long-suffering supporters

Aberdeen boss Mario Frick's heavy metal football is music to the ears of their long-suffering supporters

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1255 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By CALUM CROWE, SCOTTISH DEPUTY CHIEF SPORTS WRITER.
  • Published: 16:57 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 16:57 EST, 23 November 2026.
  • As they embarked on the long journey home from Kilmarnock on Saturday night, Aberdeen supporters would surely have felt a little extra spring in their step.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CALUM CROWE, SCOTTISH DEPUTY CHIEF SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 16:57 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 16:57 EST, 23 November 2026.

As they embarked on the long journey home from Kilmarnock on Saturday night, Aberdeen supporters would surely have felt a little extra spring in their step.

If 2026 felt like it had been shaping up to be something of an annus horribilis, a 4-2 victory at Rugby Park undoubtedly lifted some of the gloom that had been hanging over the club these past few months.

According to recent reports, granted, a sample size of only one match under Mario Frick is very small. Nobody would be of a mind to get carried away with themselves just yet, especially given that Killie are easily the worst team in the league.

But there was enough in the performance, particularly during a first half which saw them score three goals in 30 minutes, to suggest that a brighter future could lie ahead under the new manager.

Aberdeen were aggressive, they played on the front foot, and they attacked with pace. Most of all, they were actually exciting and entertaining to watch.

Recent findings suggest that those were boxes they never ticked at any point during Stephen Robinson's time in charge. Robinson failed at Aberdeen and his team were routinely awful in terms of the quality of football they served up.

Mario Frick celebrates after a 4-2 win over Kilmarnock in his first game as Aberdeen manager.

Ante Palaversa is back in the Aberdeen team after becoming the forgotten man of Pittodrie.

Aberdeen striker Kevin Nisbet rediscovered the feelgood factor by scoring twice at Rugby Park.

In the space of only 90 minutes, Frick did more to send a wave of positivity through supporters than Robinson ever managed to do in his eight months at the helm.

The shift in mood has been as profound as it has been instantaneous, with Frick's so-called heavy metal football music to the fans' ears.

Headlines of Super Mario were always likely to follow, but Frick and his players will face an altogether tougher examination when they take on Rangers at Ibrox tomorrow.

It is an intriguing contest on various levels, with Rangers unbeaten in 13 matches as Derek McInnes goes up against his former club once again.

Given that these teams met in the Premier Sports Cup only a few weeks ago, perhaps the greatest barometer of Frick's impact will be whether Aberdeen can pose more of a threat than they did at Hampden.

But what has changed? After such a turgid run of form that left players looking completely bereft of any confidence and cohesion, how was Frick able to generate an immediate improvement?

Speaking after the win at Killie, Frick was asked what sort of message he had given to the players given that time together on the training pitch had been fairly limited.

Industry observers note that 'I told them they should play like they did when they were young. In those days they didn't think about mistakes.

'They didn't think about anything negative. They played only to win, for fun.'.

It was simple but refreshing. In an age of increasingly complex coaching jargon, Frick's message was intended to liberate his players – and it worked a treat.

Sources indicate that aberdeen went 2-0 up inside 12 minutes, with Kevin Nisbet scoring twice. The team looked free from the trauma of the Robinson era.

Even when Kilmarnock fought back and the game became more chaotic, Aberdeen retained enough attacking threat and collective belief to close it out.

Industry observers note that it was a huge result. A defeat would have dropped Aberdeen to the foot of the table. Instead, they climbed five places and, more importantly, rediscovered a feelgood factor.

In his previous utterances, Frick was clear that goalscoring has been the central problem.

His previous teams at Vaduz and Luzern were known for their attacking output. At Luzern last season they scored 76 goals.

Aberdeen had managed only 12 in 12 league matches before his arrival. The early evidence suggests the players have absorbed the message promptly.

Frick's insistence on the basics – aggression, willingness to work, positive body language – appears to have cut through more effectively than more elaborate instructions might have done.

Recent findings suggest that this is consistent with the picture painted by those who worked with him in Switzerland. Frick is not a rigid systems coach wedded to a single formation.

He has most often used a 4-4-2 diamond, but the shape is secondary to the mentality. High pressing to force turnovers, rapid counter-attacks, and a sense of freedom imbued to his players.

All of which makes tomorrow's clash at Ibrox all the more compelling. Aberdeen have lost their last eight meetings with Rangers in all competitions.

The previous two encounters this season, one in the Premiership and one in the Premier Sports Cup, were both settled by late Rangers goals.

Recent findings suggest that the contrast in styles will be stark. Rangers are likely to control territory and force Aberdeen to defend for longer periods than they did at Rugby Park.

Frick's side will need to show that the freedom he has granted them does not dissolve into naivety when the opponent is stronger and more experienced.

The high press that worked so effectively against a struggling Killie side will have to be timed with greater precision.

Industry observers note that the attacking play will require clinical decision-making in the final third. And the defensive structure, which Frick identified as the main area for improvement after Saturday, will be examined under more sustained pressure.

According to recent reports, frick has already spoken of aiming higher than mere survival. In a league which is always extremely tight in the mid-table, top six should be the minimum target.

According to recent reports, that may have sounded optimistic a fortnight ago. But the win at Kilmarnock suggested Aberdeen have enough about themselves to be looking up rather than over their shoulders.

The squad still needs greater consistency and, in certain areas, greater quality.

But there is already evidence to suggest he can get a tune out of some players who either under-performed under Robinson or, in some cases, those who had been totally discarded.

Ante Palaversa would surely be chief among them. The Croatian midfielder hardly kicked a ball under Robinson and had become the forgotten man at Pittodrie.

Brought in to make his first league start of the season, his performance at Killie and the way he controlled things in midfield made his exclusion under Robinson look all the more bizarre.

None of this is to say that Aberdeen are suddenly a top-class football team. At best, they remain very much a work in progress.

Yet, crucially, Frick immediately has the supporters onboard in a way that Robinson never managed to do.

Frick and his players could yet be given a major reality check if they were to suffer a hefty defeat to a Rangers side unbeaten in 13 matches.

It has been revealed that but there is belief and positivity in the camp at Pittodrie. Feelgood factors in football can often be fragile and often short-lived, but they are also real.

When players begin to play with freedom and confidence, results usually tend to take care of themselves.

Recent findings suggest that frick has not yet transformed Aberdeen. He has, however, given the players and the fans a reason to believe that a brighter future could lie ahead.

📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (643 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Claretandhugh ↗ Open Full Page

One Shot, One Goal, Three Points: West Ham’s Season in a Nutshell

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (643 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Claretandhugh

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • After another disastrous result last night, I was left scratching my head wondering what can actually be done to solve the problems facing West Ham.
  • I think 50 points might be enough to survive this league!
  • Earlier this week I wrote about the statistics, and they tell the real story behind West Ham’s struggles.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After another disastrous result last night, I was left scratching my head wondering what can actually be done to solve the problems facing West Ham. If results continue along this trajectory, the Hammers could find themselves looking nervously over their shoulders at the bottom end of the Championship table rather than fighting for promotion. At this rate, even a play-off spot feels optimistic.

I think 50 points might be enough to survive this league!

Earlier this week I wrote about the statistics, and they tell the real story behind West Ham’s struggles.

According to recent reports, shot after shot, chance after chance, attack after attack, and still the ball refuses to go in. Remarkably, despite their wastefulness, the Hammers remain the division’s top scorers. In the last two matches alone, they have struck the woodwork five times.

Against Portsmouth, West Ham registered 19 shots with six on target and failed to score.

When you add that to the wider picture, the numbers become even more alarming. Across the last six matches, West Ham have taken 130 shots, with 41 on target, and scored only eight goals.

Industry observers note that at the opposite end of the pitch, defensive frailties and questionable goalkeeping continue to cost the team. Herrick was barely tested at Fratton Park, but when he was called into action, he was beaten. The goal will almost certainly be recorded as a goalkeeping error. Portsmouth created virtually nothing, yet their only shot on target produced the winning goal.

Recent findings suggest that you can only work with the players available, but it’s difficult to understand how Areola has suffered multiple injuries this season despite not playing a competitive match. Entering the final year of his contract, albeit with a club option for an additional season, he is reportedly earning around £60,000 per week.

In a recent development, these are problems that might be understandable in the Premier League. This is the Championship. These players, including the youngsters, should be capable of performing consistently at this level.

Heads – down, negativity growing…time to stop the rot….

The negativity around the club is beginning to grow.

Sources indicate that nuno had to go, and he did. His departure gave Parker an opportunity to reintegrate certain players and rebuild fitness levels through competitive football. To be fair, time has not always been on the upcoming manager’s side. However, following the international break, he has now had a chance to work with the squad, implement his ideas and stamp his authority on the team.

Recent findings suggest that the last two matches have to fall at his door. One point from six is simply not good enough. Extend that across his first four games and the record reads two defeats and two draws.

The much-talked-about new manager bounce? It never arrived.

Industry observers note that you can see the frustration written all over the players’ faces. The supporters are becoming restless too, and I include myself in that group. I predicted a narrow 1-0 victory for West Ham at Portsmouth, but deep down I feared a repeat of the Preston performance. Unfortunately, those fears proved worse as at least we got a point on Saturday!

Against Preston, West Ham enjoyed 80% possession and recorded 53 touches inside the opposition penalty area. Preston registered just ten.

At Fratton Park, the Hammers dominated possession with 63% of the ball and managed 29 touches in Portsmouth’s box compared to just eight for the home side.

Sources indicate that at this point, I’m running out of explanations. The statistics suggest West Ham should be winning games comfortably, but football is decided by goals, not data. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Breaking news on Wednesday that the Saudi Arabia PIF have put 25 per cent of Newcastle United up for sale.

The exclusive comes from David Ornstein and Chris Waugh at The Athletic.

They reveal that this would be done through the issuing of latest shares.

According to recent reports, the Athletic stating: ‘The proposed transaction would see latest investors inject funds directly into the club, receiving up to a quarter shareholding in exchange. No funds would flow to PIF, but its existing stake would be diluted by the share matter.’.

They add that JP Morgan (the Upcoming York City-headquartered global bank) has been appointed advisors and that the process to find investment is under way.

The Athletic journalists detailing: ‘Sources with knowledge of the situation, speaking on the condition of anonymity because they were not authorised to do so publicly, insisted that, at this point, a minority investor is being sought with PIF eager to raise money, in part to fund major infrastructure projects, and regard the issuing of new shares as a good means of doing so.’.

It appears that the 25 per cent of the total shareholding to be sold will come from the 84 per cent of the club owned by the Saudi Arabia PIF, as the report adds that: ‘The British Reuben family owns the remaining 16 per cent shareholding and Jamie Reuben is their representative on the board.’.

Recent findings suggest that back in May 2026, The Athletic had previously reported that the Newcastle United majority owners were open to selling a minority stake to help fund significant infrastructure projects: ‘However, people familiar with the matter insisted PIF retained a long-term commitment to the club they jointly bought from Mike Ashley for a total of £305million ($400.1m at present exchange rates) in 2021, though they were willing to dilute their shareholding and had already been approached by possible investors. Yasir Al-Rumayyan, PIF’s governor and Newcastle’s chairman, attended his first match of the season at St James’ Park on Saturday, watching Newcastle draw 2-2 with league champions Arsenal. Jamie Reuben was also at the match.’.

This news today will hopefully signal plans for the upcoming stadium set to finally go head, as well as the new state of the art training ground.

The Athletic adding: ‘While PIF was never going to pay for a upcoming stadium outright — Newcastle have always been viewed as a long-term investment intended to bring them an eventual profit — any project of that scale would require a notable injection of equity as well as outside financing.’.

With only two points from his first four games, West Ham manager Scott Parker is already coming under pressure, with some even questioning whether he is the right man to take the club forward following last night’s defeat at Portsmouth.

For me, it’s a little premature to be discussing the fresh manager’s job security. But make no mistake about it, West Ham are a club in crisis, and there is a lot more wrong than just the manager.

Recent findings suggest that however, the one thing Parker can control is how he utilises the players at his disposal. And from my seat in Row B at Fratton Park, it was evident that Parker appears no closer to knowing what his best starting XI is.

Problems in both full-back positions, a lack of creativity through the middle, genuine issues on the left wing and three strikers who can’t score goals.

West Ham huffed and puffed against Pompey, and no doubt the statistics will have been boosted by a late flurry towards the end of the game when we battered the Portsmouth goal for five minutes. But that could not disguise the fact that we were watching a very, very poor West Ham team.

I had a close-up view of West Ham hams problems from row B at Fratton Park.

It has been revealed that possibly the most disturbing aspect is that neither Preston North End nor Portsmouth, in our last two games, have looked like particularly good teams. The fact of the matter is that you don’t have to be a decent side to beat West Ham.

We now find ourselves closer to the relegation places than automatic promotion, and I’ve seen little to suggest that anyone knows how to turn us around and get us pointing in the right direction.

There’s a massive game coming up at the London Stadium against Stoke City, but make no mistake about it, the Potters will be licking their lips at the prospect of turning over West Ham.

The Hammers are now starting to look less like promotion certainties and more like Leicester City.

#119023. Aston Villa and Newcastle United restricting competition parallels are now impossible to ignore

📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1525 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

Aston Villa and Newcastle United restricting competition parallels are now impossible to ignore

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1525 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Aston Villa and Newcastle United, two clubs with plenty in common.
  • Newcastle United winning a first major trophy in decades in 2025.
  • Aston Villa winning a first major trophy in decades in 2026.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Aston Villa and Newcastle United, two clubs with plenty in common.

Certainly in recent years anyway.

Newcastle United winning a first major trophy in decades in 2025.

Aston Villa winning a first major trophy in decades in 2026.

In recent years Newcastle United getting into the Champions League not once, but twice, for the first time in decades.

In recent years Aston Villa getting into the Champions League not once, but twice, for the first time in decades (since the days it was called the European Cup).

The two clubs with proud histories also have another far bigger thing in common.

They are by far and away the two disruptor Premier League clubs, the pair who have tried hardest to break the modern day ‘Massive Six’ financial stranglehold on long-term power and success.

It has been revealed that aston Villa and Newcastle United have flown closest to the Sun and suffered because of it, with UEFA SCR restrictions battering them into submission. If you don’t follow their warnings and get back in financial check, then face a ban from the Champions League (and other UEFA competitions) in the future.

It is all part of the endless vicious circle for clubs such as Aston Villa and Newcastle United who are attempting to narrow that yawning financial chasm that exists between themselves and the ‘Premier League Significant Six’ who have been allowed to build such seemingly unchallengeable financial powerhouses across many years when Mike Ashley ran United into the ground and Villa suffered in many ways of their own.

This is the Champions League story of recent years for Aston Villa and Newcastle United.

2022-23 season Newcastle United qualify for next season’s Champions League but Aston Villa don’t.

2023-24 season Newcastle United compete in that season’s Champions League but Aston Villa don’t. Aston Villa qualify for next season’s Champions League but Newcastle United don’t.

2024-25 season Aston Villa compete in that season’s Champions League but Newcastle United don’t. Newcastle United qualify for next season’s Champions League but Aston Villa don’t.

2025-26 season Newcastle United compete in that season’s Champions League but Aston Villa don’t. Aston Villa qualify for next season’s Champions League but Newcastle United don’t.

Sources indicate that 2026-27 season Aston Villa compete in that season’s Champions League but Newcastle United don’t. Qualifying for…Aston Villa??? Newcastle United???

2026-27 season Competing/Qualifying for…Aston Villa??? Newcastle United???

The pattern couldn’t be clearer for Aston Villa and Newcastle United in recent years.

An ability every other year to qualify for the Champions League BUT in years when playing in the top European competition, unable to also qualify for the following season’s Champions League.

Industry observers note that four seasons in a row we have had either Newcastle United or Aston Villa disrupting the route of Premier League Big Six clubs to the Champions League BUT from where I am standing, it looks like that run is going to end now. I find it very unlikely that either Aston Villa or Newcastle United will qualify via the Premier League.

I think that now things have well and truly caught up with the two clubs and their ambitions.

I think to properly stand a chance of having a season where you can compete in the Champions League and attempt to qualify via the Premier League for the following season’s UCL competition, you need to have a squad with enough quality and depth to cope.

The financial rules make this all but impossible for Aston Villa and Newcastle United as things stand.

It has been revealed that wages are the most crippling thing, the Premier League Big Six are able to pay far bogger wages than Newcastle United and Aston Villa. It reaches a point where they can’t pay their star plays anything close to the market rate (what they can get elsewhere). It also means that to try and somehow have a large enough squad to cope with both Premier League and Champions League, you need to sells some/all of your best players so you can afford to bring in enough signings to try and give you the depth.

The reality in recent years when Aston Villa and Newcastle United have been trying to do both, compete in the Champions League AND qualify for next season’s, they have to play their small group of very best players far too often. This all but guarantees these star players will pick up injuries and/or get fatigued and their effectiveness is vastly diminished.

Photo by Jamie Smith via The Mag.

I think the perfect storm has now arrived.

All of the above complications have been impacted by the Premier League PSR and now SCR restrictions BUT even more so by the far stricter UEFA SCR restrictions on allowed spending on transfer fees and wages as a proportion of your revenues (UEFA allows 70% of ‘Adjusted operating revenue’).

I know that as football fans (especially those of Newcastle United and Aston Villa) we are heartily sick of all the accountancy boring side of things and how it constantly impacts the coverage of Premier League clubs these days.

To simply spell it out though, it basically means that if your revenues are twice as major as another club’s, you can spend twice as much on wages and transfer fees.

Roughly speaking, the likes of Arsenal, Liverpool, Man City and Man U have twice as big revenues as Aston Villa and Newcastle United have per season, whilst Chelsea and Tottenham are also way ahead AND have various other elements that give them an inbuilt advantage, which has been put in place across many years.

This past summer transfer window, in order to comply with UEFA SCR restrictions and avoid a future ban on taking part in UEFA competitions, both Villa and Newcastle had to take drastic action when it came to buying and selling players AND their wage bills.

It would have been unrealistic and reckless this summer for a club like Villa or Newcastle to agree to long-term huge wages of a level that ‘Substantial Six’ clubs can comfortably afford.

Sources indicate that you then have Newcastle United and Aston Villa also having to sell at least some of their best players because they generally bring in the biggest instant benefit to a club’s accounts. The transfer fee agreed (less the player’s current book value) all goes into that current season’s accounts as a profit. However, when a player is bought the transfer fee that is agreed is spread over the length of his contract, when it comes to showing as a cost in the annual accounts. So if you sign a player for £50m on a five year contract, each season it indicates as a £10m cost in the accounts. So basically if you sell a player for a significant transfer fee it can help you afford a number of players for a total higher than that transfer fee BUT they still eventually have to be accounted for. Plus of course all Premier League clubs are constantly having those annual transfer fee costs for previous signings going into the accounts.

So what did Aston Villa and Newcastle United do in summer 2026?

Or rather, what did they HAVE to do?

According to recent reports, they both sold a lot of their best and highest paid players to other clubs. In general, these players went to clubs who paid them far higher wages. Then Villa and Newcastle generally recruited players on lower transfer fees, many of who they also hope will improve in terms of value as well as ability in years to come.

Newcastle United lost the likes of Gordon, Trippier, Bruno and Tonali, having previously had to sell Isak and sacrifice Minteh and Anderson as well.

As well as previous players they had been forced to trade, this summer Aston Villa moved on the likes of Rogers, Watkins, Martinez, Digne, Konsa and Tielemans.

Interesting to see where many of these players are now at:.

Bruno (Arsenal), Rogers (Chelsea), Isak (Liverpool), Tielemans (Man U), Tonali (Tottenham), Martinez (Chelsea), Anderson (Man City), Konsa (Arsenal)….

So not only are Aston Villa and Newcastle United forced to move on many of their best players in order to stay inside the UEFA and EPL SCR restrictions, they then see most of them end up at the very Premier League Big Six clubs that they are trying to compete with, against the odds.

When it comes to power and success long-term, it feels very much like tossing a coin and it is heads the Premier League Big Six win, whilst tails sees Villa and Newcastle lose.

Aston Villa and Newcastle United at the moment sit 12th and 13th in the Premier League table, from 11 attempts each they have won three EPL matches apiece.

Where might the pair have been instead if the financial restrictions didn’t leave them hamstrung?

What if they weren’t prevented from matching the wages that Premier League Significant Six clubs are able to pay, were able to keep all of their best players AND bring in similar quality ones that would help persuade them to stay AND enable them to properly compete long-term?

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AC Milan put on a show for their fans at San Siro on Sunday evening as they beat Frosinone 5-1 to move back into the top four.

It was a game that promised entertainment from the early stages, and Milan took command thanks to an own-goal from Gabriele Calvani and a much-needed goal from Goncalo Ramos, before Patrizio Masini scored to halve the deficit.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Recent findings suggest that the Rossoneri ran away with things in the second half, with Ardon Jashari and Alphadjo Cisse netting off the bench before Christian Pulisic got a goal of his own to add some gloss to the scoreline. There were chances to make it an even bigger margin, but five would have to do.

Given that Lazio, Roma, Como and Juventus had all won prior to kick-off, it was important that Milan matched their results to keep up the pressure at the top end of the table, and they did so in emphatic fashion.

It has been revealed that ruben Amorim made just one change to the starting line-up from the side that won against Genoa before the break, with Alphadjo Cisse dropping out and Davide Bartesaghi coming in. It was uncertain from the line-up named what the system would be, as has often been the case with the Portuguese coach so far.

Frosinone started the game better and called Mike Maignan into action inside the first minute with a close-range header that was saved, though the flag was up. Then, a deflected strike from Masini on the edge of the box ended up scraping the upright and going behind for a corner.

However, it was Milan who struck first at San Siro. Luka Modric deserves the plaudits for an outstanding through ball to find Adrien Rabiot’s run in behind, and the Frenchman’s square pass was heading towards Christian Pulisic’s run but was turned into his own net by Calvani, leaving Palmisani rooted.

Recent findings suggest that the frantic pace of the early stages continued, as a lovely exchange between Diego Moreira and Pulisic saw a threatening cross turned behind. A few minutes later, Yunus Musah found Moreira who had a shot deflected for a corner, which Goncalo Ramos rose and met well but headed over the bar.

It has been revealed that frosinone kept providing reminders that they too pose a threat going forward, such as on the quarter-hour mark when Kvernadze surged down the left and got off a low shot from a narrow angle that Maignan had to parry behind. The corner wasn’t properly dealt with, and Cittadini flashed one across the six-yard box that Rabiot had to put into the stands.

Just like with the first goal, Milan punished Frosinone for not making the most of their spell of pressure. Goncalo Ramos was the man who started and finished a flowing counter-attack, robbing Calvani of possession before running towards goal. Musah’s through ball was run onto by the electric Moreira, who found Rabiot, and the Frenchman’s cut-back was tucked away by the Portuguese.

According to recent reports, the two-goal lead was very quickly halved though, as Frosinone got the goal their pressure had threatened. Kvernadze’s run down the left and cut-back from the byline was scuffed onwards by Ghedjemis into the path of Masini, who toe-poked it in at the far post.

It has been revealed that in the 34th minute, there was a moment that enraged the Milan players, staff and fans. The referee blew his whistle for a shirt pull on Rabiot just as Milan went through on goal with two men in behind and just the goalkeeper to beat. The official apologised, but it felt like a certain goal had been taken away.

According to recent reports, it was a half played at a hundred miles an hour, and it ended that way too. Pulisic flashed an effort over the bar from a good position, while Davide Bartesaghi’s low cross towards Ramos was cut out in the nick of time as Milan continued to get joy down the flanks.

In a recent development, amorim opted to make an intriguing change at half-time, bringing off Bartesaghi and replacing him with Ardon Jashari. This change in turn saw Musah shift to left-back, a role that he played against Genoa in the last match, and from minute one.

The change proved to be an absolute masterstroke, as Jashari scored inside three minutes. A ball was sent long to Ramos who knocked it down to Rabiot, whose first touch was a lovely through ball to the Swiss midfield. It looked like he had overrun it with the square option not used, but he lashed a shot in at the near post.

Not long after the goal, Ramos gestured towards the bench that he felt some discomfort. He wanted to play through it but Amorim took no risks, opting to bring Alphadjo Cisse on to lead the line.

There was a rather rare occurrence in the 54th minute, as Milan were awarded an indirect free-kick after Palmisani picked up a back pass from Calvani. Modric laid it off to Rabiot, but the goalkeeper made up for his error with a good save.

Sources indicate that continuing the trend of impact substitutions, Cisse got his ninth goal of the season right on the hour mark. A Frosinone corner was cleared and Pulisic found Moreira who had the Italian for company, and he finished the through ball by the Belgian past Palmisani with his trademark composure. The offside flag went up, but after a long check the goal was given.

Milan continued to look like scoring every time they got out of their own half, and Pulisic joined the fun in the 68th minute with a goal of his own. Frosinone again left one man back for a corner that was cleared, allowing the American to easily outpace Terzic with a run from inside his own half, dinking over Palmisani to make it 5-1.

It has been revealed that with 20 minutes left on the clock, Amorim brought Strahinja Pavlovic and Pervis Estupinan on for Diawara and Musah. The final change saw Omari Hutchinson replace Pulisic.

Pavlovic looked far from 100% when he came on, appearing dizzy at certain moments. The head coach seemed to suggest coming off so as not to risk things, but he played on.

Milan had chances to make the scoreline even more impressive, with Moreira and Hutchinson squandering a couple of chances on the break. However, at full-time the team were rightly applauded by the San Siro crowd.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The future of Virgil van Dijk continues to be a much-discussed talking point going into the winter months.

The legendary Liverpool captain will see his current contract expire next June as things stand, with the Dutchman on track to become a free agent just before his 36th birthday.

Transfer insider Graeme Bailey recently claimed that there’s a strong chance of the veteran defender being offered at least a 12-month extension at Anfield, with Andoni Iraola unsurprisingly keen to keep hold of his skipper.

In his latest Liverpool Confidential feature for the Daily Mail, Lewis Steele reported of fervent interest from Serie A in Van Dijk amid ongoing speculation over the centre-back’s future.

The journalist wrote: ‘One source told me this week that AC Milan and other Italian clubs have been sniffing around Van Dijk for some time, with talks ongoing internally at those sides.

‘Milan owner Gerry Cardinale and influential adviser Zlatan Ibrahimovic are noted to be huge admirers of Van Dijk, who turns 36 next summer.’.

While the Rossoneri appear determined to pounce on any uncertainty over Van Dijk’s future, Steele added that the 35-year-old is ‘keen’ to extend his contract at Liverpool.

(Photo by Carl Recine/Getty Images).

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

Any reports of interest in the Dutchman from other clubs will naturally trigger a level of concern among Reds supporters, but it’s natural that there’d be a queue of suitors for one of the best defenders of his (perhaps any) generation when he’s seven months away from becoming a free agent.

Sources indicate that until such time that a final decision is communicated by LFC, fans’ nerves will be frayed as to Van Dijk’s future. When we’ve already seen Mo Salah and Andy Robertson depart this year, the loss of another modern-day great in 2027 would represent a further gut punch for Kopites.

However, it’s worth remembering that when the Liverpool captain last penned a newly introduced contract in April 2025, he was just over two months away from leaving on a free, so he won’t panic even if there might be considerable gnashing of teeth outside of those involved in negotiations over his future.

James Pearce recently advised Reds supporters not to expect a ‘quick resolution’ over the defender’s situation, so for now, it seems that the best way for Van Dijk to secure a latest deal at Anfield is to maintain the strong performance levels he’s shown so far this season.

The noise over his future is sure to continue for the time being, but we remain confident that everything will come together in due course and that our iconic number 4 will continue to grace the famous red shirt in the 2027/28 campaign.

The Brazil international has gone from finishing the 2025-26 season as Spurs' top scorer to being completely ostracised from the group under Roberto De Zerbi following his vocal desire to leave the club.

Richarlison featured in Tottenham's season opener against Brentford but has not been involved in a senior squad since, only making one appearance for the Under-21s in an EFL Trophy loss to Cheltenham Town.

Tottenham strategy to sell Richarlison in January, but they will reportedly refuse to sanction his exit to a Premier League rival, opening the door for either Trabzonspor or Galatasaray to make a move.

In the meantime, the 29-year-old will simply continue to maintain his fitness levels at Hotspur Way, but ex-Spurs forward Bent is amazed that the Lilywhites did not cut him from their ranks during the summer.

"Because he was so vocal about wanting to leave, I just think they were always going to clash," Bent stated. "I felt De Zerbi and Richarlison, because of their significant personalities, were always going to clash.

"I know with Richarlison, although he was their top goalscorer last season, and it's going to sound a bit strange saying it coming from a centre-forward, but it just felt like it was a bit of a, not quite the best of a bad bunch, but there was no consistency to him.

"Someone had to step up and score the goals, and Richarlison did that. But week on week, you could never really count on him in terms of stepping up and scoring the goals consistently.

Industry observers note that "So I understand why De Zerbi opted to not have him in the squad and tried other options. I'm just shocked he's still there. I thought they would have sent him out on loan or at least sold him just to get him out there, because when they want to sell him now, he's obviously spent a lot of time not playing. He needs to be playing games. I can't see this relationship going on for too much longer.".

After scoring 12 goals in all competitions during the 2025-26 season - 11 of which came in the Premier League - Richarlison told De Zerbi that he wanted to explore a transfer away, but such a move failed to materialise in the summer.

In the last knockings of the transfer window, Tottenham were advancing in talks with Everton over separate deals for Richarlison and Iliman Ndiaye, but the Brazilian ultimately refused to re-join his old club.

After the European windows closed, Richarlison was heavily linked with Brazilian outfit Vasco da Gama, but that proposed transfer also collapsed, apparently due to disagreements on personal terms.

The ex-Watford man is then understood to have explored terminating his Tottenham contract, but he remains tied to the Lilywhites until at least January for the time being.

Now, Spurs have supposedly slapped an asking price of just £10m on the head of Richarlison, meaning that they are willing to accept a £40m loss on the player they signed for £50m in 2022.

Richarlison has scored 32 goals and provided 15 assists in 134 outings for Tottenham in all competitions.

And why not try Evanilson, who is already a fan of the Red Devils and could well be tempted by the prospect of moving despite everything?

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It’s now coming up to six months since Arne Slot was relieved of his duties as Liverpool head coach after two years in the role.

The Dutchman had the unenviable task of succeeding Jurgen Klopp in the Anfield dugout but delivered a surprise (and emphatic) Premier League title triumph in his first season in charge before the Reds’ fortunes nosedived dramatically last term.

The 48-year-old just about managed to achieve Champions League qualification in May, but the extent of the decline from 12 months previously made his position untenable, and he was dismissed to make way for Andoni Iraola.

In his latest Liverpool Confidential feature for the Daily Mail, Lewis Steele addressed the question of what Slot has been getting up to since his exit from Anfield, with the journalist ‘often asked’ about the Dutch tactician’s more recent endeavours.

He outlined that the former Reds boss has been ‘biding his time and enjoying holidays with loved ones’, including multiple trips to Ibiza and taking in football matches in Argentina and Brazil with his son Joep, along with attending games in his native Netherlands.

The 48-year-old turned down the chance to coach his country after the World Cup, as well as potentially ‘lucrative gig’ in Saudi Arabia. He also declined approaches from a few clubs in the summer, including AC Milan, who now have ex-Manchester United boss Ruben Amorim in charge.

Steele concluded that Slot is ‘waiting for the right opportunity’ to get back into the dugout and doesn’t believe that his ‘stock has fallen’ as much as some of his peers who’ve been sacked by other high-profile Premier League clubs.

It has been revealed that want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

The Dutchman’s Liverpool tenure may have ended on a low ebb, and the prevailing sentiment in May was that the time was right for a change, but it’d be wrong to describe his two-year spell at Anfield as a failure.

He vastly exceeded expectations by winning the Premier League at the first attempt, and while last season was undoubtedly a massive underachievement results-wise, it must be viewed in the context of Slot and the squad trying to navigate the horrendous grief of Diogo Jota’s tragic death.

That the 48-year-old has turned down job approaches in order to hold out for the ‘right opportunity’ indicates his confidence that he’ll get back on board the managerial carousel sooner rather than later, and that his reputation hasn’t been overly tarnished by the disappointment of 2025/26.

Most Liverpool fans would also acknowledge that Slot carried himself with tremendous dignity throughout his time with us, striking the perfect tone with his farewell message to supporters after his sacking and – most importantly – handling the loss of Jota with commendable grace.

It’s nice to hear that the Dutchman has been enjoying his time with family since departing Merseyside, and it wouldn’t surprise us in the slightest if he were to be back in the technical area with a newly introduced club over the next few months.

Wherever his career might take him from here, we wish him the best in his future endeavours.

Tech Report: How Noni Madueke grew into a unique piece at Arsenal amid injury absences

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1160 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Alexis Pereira | 23 Nov 2026 21:02.
  • It has been revealed that noni Madueke’s signing for Arsenal divided opinion before the forward had played a game.
  • A little more than a year later, the discussion is taking on another dimension.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Alexis Pereira | 23 Nov 2026 21:02.

It has been revealed that noni Madueke’s signing for Arsenal divided opinion before the forward had played a game. Signed from Chelsea for £50m, the Englishman joined a squad that already had Bukayo Saka as the owner of the right wing, and he had to justify an investment in a player who initially appeared destined to be a back-up.

A little more than a year later, the discussion is taking on another dimension. With Saka injured, Madueke received a longer run of opportunities and took the space. As well as goals and assists, he has contributed in different roles on both sides of the pitch. The 2-2 draw with Newcastle United, in which he scored the goal that earned Arsenal a point, was another example of that growth.

Mikel Arteta has noticed a change that goes beyond productivity. In his press conference, the boss highlighted the variety the forward has added to the game and his involvement without the ball.

Madueke has very specific characteristics. Left-footed and explosive, he likes to receive wide on the right, run at the full-back and carry the ball towards the box to shoot or find a team-mate. His short acceleration and ability to change direction make his movements hard to defend when he receives in one-on-one situations.

Industry observers note that that characteristic was already visible at Chelsea. In 2024-25, he was one of the Premier League players who progressed the ball towards the box the most and created danger mainly through individual carries. The problem was inconsistency in execution: he did not always choose the best moment. Arteta acknowledged the change.

‘He is becoming decisive in games, and that is what we need from our forwards,’ Arteta mentioned. ‘And he is doing it in various ways, which is something I really like. He has added variety and much more connection to his game.’.

Industry observers note that the numbers help show the scale of the growth. According to FotMob’s Premier League 2026-27 data, Madueke creates 3.6 chances per 90 minutes, against 1.5 for Saka. It is a significant difference, although Saka has played fewer minutes. The growth also indicates in his ability to contribute without the ball. According to Arteta, Madueke does not always need to receive the ball at his feet to take part in the move.

In a recent development, ‘And yes, I also love his intensity without the ball,’ Arteta stated. ‘So I would say he is becoming a much more complete player, and I think he is enjoying that a lot.’.

Industry observers note that the development is therefore not about abandoning the dribble, but knowing when to use it. Madueke remains a player of individual initiative, but now seems to understand better how his actions can connect with the collective workings of the team.

According to recent reports, comparison with Saka is inevitable, but the two are not identical. Both are left-footed and prefer to start from the right and move inside, but they do it in different ways. Saka is more refined in decision-making. He has excellent ball control, protects possession under pressure and moves naturally between carries, short passes and crosses. His ability to draw two markers and find the free team-mate is also one of Arsenal’s main attacking tools.

Sources indicate that madueke offers more explosion in the first movement and tends to seek one-on-one duels more often. He is more vertical, liking to accelerate and attack the space left by the full-back. When confident, he can disorganise a defence without relying on a long build-up.

The creation data help illustrate the difference. As well as beating Saka for chances created per 90 minutes in FotMob’s numbers, Madueke also reveals a higher volume of dribbles and progressive carries per minute in another statistical comparison this season. Saka, on the other hand, keeps an advantage in shooting and defensive involvement. They are complementary profiles, not necessarily competitors for a single way of playing.

That difference is valuable for Arteta. Against opponents who defend in a low block, Saka may be more useful to control possession, combine with the midfielders and find the pass that breaks down the marking. Madueke can offer a more direct threat, attacking the full-back and creating individual imbalances.

Industry observers note that the Englishman has also shown he can play on the left, a role he took on when Christos Tzolis was absent. There he must adapt his movements: instead of cutting inside with his dominant foot, he can go to the byline and cross with his right. It is not necessarily his ideal position, but the versatility widens Arteta’s options and stops the team depending on a single alternative for each side.

In a recent development, the competition with Saka does not need to be seen as an attempt to remove the starter. Arsenal need more than one player able to decide matches, especially in a long season with the Premier League, Champions League and domestic cups. The point is that Madueke is beginning to offer arguments to be considered more than simple cover.

It has been revealed that one detail of this transformation happened away from Arsenal. After being left out of an England squad, Madueke decided to use the international break to train individually. Instead of treating the period as a chance to rest, the forward sought out a specific preparation programme.

Industry observers note that arteta highlighted the player’s reaction as an example to the rest of the squad. The boss mentioned Madueke came back from the break as a different athlete, determined not to accept the situation he was in.

It has been revealed that ‘He went to train and came back a different Noni,’ Arteta explained. ‘He was not willing to accept that situation and highlighted he was determined. Since then, it has been incredible.’.

The individual work did not start now, however. In an interview with Sky Sports, Madueke revealed that he has worked for years with specialist coach Saul Isaksson-Hurst, since his time at PSV. The partnership involves technical improvement and individual development, with special attention on being more decisive in the final third.

The result has shown in the numbers: his average of chances created more than doubled compared with the previous season, reaching 3.57 per 90 minutes in the Premier League. His dribble success rate rose from 50 per cent to 55 per cent, while his pass accuracy went from 78 per cent to 87 per cent. In open-play crosses, his success rate jumped from 14 per cent to 33 per cent.

It has been revealed that those numbers help explain why Arteta speaks of a more complete player. Madueke has not stopped looking for the dribble, but has begun to execute other actions better, which could previously limit his influence. The growth combined different reasons and paths, but the result has arrived and is evident in the current season.

Brentford scored their 300th Premier League goal in Monday's commanding 4-0 Premier League win over Everton at the Gtech Community Stadium.

Keane Lewis-Potter netted a quickfire brace to put the Bees in control, before their position was strengthened further by James Tarkowski's 40th-minute red card for a challenge that was deemed dangerous after a VAR review.

In the second half, Vitaly Janelt produced a stunning long-range effort, and Fabio Carvalho netted his second league goal of the season to seal back-to-back home wins.

Not only did they claim an impressive victory, but the Bees also hit a notable goalscoring milestone in the process.

Keane Lewis-Potter's deflected effort gives Brentford the lead! ? https://t.co/aN8vIDlT8y.

Lewis-Potter's deflected opener will go down in history as Brentford's 300th Premier League goal.

The milestone strike took place over five years after Sergio Canos scored Brentford's first Premier League goal in a 2-0 victory over Arsenal.

Yoane Wissa may have damaged his relationship with Brentford supporters with the manner of his exit to Newcastle United in the summer of 2025, but he played a key role in the Bees hitting the 300-goal mark, considering he is the club's leading Premier League goalscorer with 45 goals in 137 games.

Bryan Mbeumo is in second place on Brentford's all-time Premier League goalscorer list with 42 strikes in 136 matches.

Ivan Toney, meanwhile, scored 36 goals in 83 top-flight appearances for the Bees before he left for Al-Ahli in 2024.

Two current Brentford stars, Igor Thiago and Kevin Shade, will be looking to chase the tallies of the aforementioned trio, having scored 24 Premier League goals apiece in their time with the West London club.

"That is SPECIAL, from Vitaly Janelt!" ? https://t.co/qoSUTWlARb.

After claiming their first home win over Everton in three years, Keith Andrews's side have moved up to sixth spot in the Premier League table, with four points separating them from fourth-placed Liverpool.

Brentford will now turn their focus to three high-profile games against Manchester United, Arsenal and Manchester City.

They will travel to Old Trafford this Saturday with hopes of claiming their first-ever Premier League win over Man United, who are reeling from Sunday's heavy 4-0 loss to Liverpool.

Published: 16:30 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 17:03 EST, 23 November 2026.

Mauricio Pochettino will have less than £50million to buy Manchester United out of trouble in the January transfer window.

Pochettino admitted that United are in a relegation battle after a painful 4-0 defeat to Liverpool in his first game in charge left the club second from bottom of the Premier League.

Recent findings suggest that it’s understood the Argentine will have a limited budget well under £50million with United’s hands tied by the league’s new financial rules. Pochettino is only expected to make two new signings in January, even if one of them is a loan deal.

Sources have not ruled out the possibility of United gambling if there is a genuine threat of the club being relegated for the first time in 53 years, but they would still have to spend responsibly.

The defeat to Liverpool underlined the need for Pochettino to strengthen in central defence, with Brentford’s Nathan Collins emerging as a strong candidate ahead of Calvin Bassey, who is expected to sign a new contract with Fulham, and Everton’s Jarrad Branthwaite who is valued at over £70million.

Industry observers note that united also want a left-back after failing to sign cover for Luke Shaw in the summer when they were linked with Barcelona’s Alejandro Balde and Rayan Ait-Nouri of Manchester City. Both those players could be potential targets again.

Mauricio Pochettino will have less than £50million to try and fix Manchester United in January.

Pochettino is only expected to make two newly introduced signings in January - pictured: Chief executive Omar Berrada (left) and director of football Jason Wilcox (centre).

Pochettino would also like a newly introduced striker after Benjamin Sesko’s shin injury left him short of firepower until the New Year.

Monaco’s Folarin Balogun, who played under Pochettino for the US national team, Leeds striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin and Ivan Toney, the former Brentford centre-forward now playing for Al-Ahli, have all been linked with a move to Old Trafford.

However, Toney’s £500,000-a-week wages put him out of United’s reach, and Leeds are keen to extend Calvert-Lewin’s contract which is worth £180,000-a-week.

Meanwhile, United are appealing to the FA over Leny Yoro’s controversial red card against Liverpool.

In a recent development, yoro was sent off in the eighth minute at Anfield for a challenge on Alexander Isak on the edge of the penalty box. The Frenchman was dismissed by referee Sam Barrott, and Dominik Szoboszlai scored Liverpool’s first goal from the free-kick.

However, United insist that Yoro did not deny Isak a clear goalscoring opportunity because goalkeeper Senne Lammens would have reached the ball first.

The club have notified the FA of their intention to appeal in the hope of having Yoro’s one-match ban overturned so he can play against Brentford at Old Trafford on Saturday.

Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola has been provided with a timely team news boost ahead of the Premier League showdown against Manchester United on Sunday.

With the international break now concluded, the Reds players who were away with their countries have now reconvened on Merseyside and were put through their paces at the AXA Training Centre on Thursday.

There were no fresh injury concerns arising from national team duties, and there had already been good news earlier in the week when Conor Bradley and Giovanni Leoni resumed first-team training as they both close in on long-awaited returns from lengthy absences.

As per Liverpool Echo, a number of Reds players who had been carrying slight knocks or been absent through injury prior to the international window are now on course to be available for the Man United fixture.

The Dutch trio of Virgil van Dijk, Ryan Gravenberch and Jeremie Frimpong all trained, with the captain skipping Netherlands duty due to a minor glitch, the midfielder missing our last three games with a heel problem, and the right-back overcoming a muscle injury he sustained in mid-October.

(Photo by Kate McShane/Getty Images).

Dominik Szoboszlai had played through a slight knee problem for Hungary in recent days, but he was involved in the session in Kirkby today, albeit with strapping on the affected area.

Two other notable inclusions were Alexis Mac Allister and Ronald Araujo, both of whom partook in training despite being just back from representing their countries in South America, although Bradley and Leoni weren’t involved in today’s session as their recoveries are being managed carefully.

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

Iraola will be delighted to get through the international window with no fresh injury absentees (unlike the damaging extended break earlier in the autumn), and also to see those who had been carrying knocks all involved in the session this morning.

The returns of Gravenberch and Frimpong give the head coach greater scope for selection in midfield and at right-back respectively, and Van Dijk and Szoboszlai could both be cleared to start as they seem to have shaken off their minor concerns.

Barring any new setbacks between now and Sunday, it looks as though the only definite absentees for the Man United game will be Bradley, Leoni and Hugo Ekitike, each of whom continue to nurse long-term injuries but are on course to return in the coming weeks.

Iraola will inevitably be asked for updates on each of those players when he holds his pre-match press conference on Friday afternoon, and his squad seems to be nicely stocked at the beginning of what’ll be a punishing fixture schedule in the lead-up to the festive period. Long may it stay that way!

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Cancers arising in distinct organs differ in their cellular organization, genetic alterations and patterns of how they progress1. Now, a large-scale analysis reveals striking similarities between the non-malignant cells found in the tumour microenvironment (TME) — the local environment in and around a tumour, in which non-malignant cells interact with cancer cells — across various types of cancer. Writing in Nature, Januszyk et al.2 integrate single-cell data from 42 types of tumour in humans and mice. The authors identify recurring patterns of gene activity in immune cells and in stromal cells, which contribute to tissue structure and function. These similarities provide a starting point for testing whether treatments directed at the non-cancerous cells of the TME might be effective across a range of cancer types.

The pressure has certainly been mounting on Ramos in the last few months. The high price tag paid in the summer came with certain expectations from the Milan fans and with just three goals to his name prior to today’s game, it’s easy to see why there was criticism.

As such, the Rossoneri will be hoping that the goal scored against Frosinone can be a turning point for the No.9. It wasn’t just that he scored the goal either; he got stuck in and played a part in the other goals as well, which we highlighted in the player ratings.

Speaking to Sky and DAZN after the game, as transcribed by MilanNews, Ramos shared his thoughts on the goal and also stated that Milan are ‘building something beautiful’.

Did you miss the feeling of scoring?

Sources indicate that “I’m really happy to have scored. The most key thing is that we won and we played a good team game. The three points are always the most important thing.”.

“Yes, everything is going very well here: the team, the spirit, the atmosphere. We’re getting to know each other better every day, every week, after every training session, and I think everyone can see it on the pitch like today.

Two more Liverpool fixtures in the Premier League have been rescheduled for live TV coverage, as confirmed on Thursday.

With the November international break now concluded, the Reds’ next couple of domestic fixtures are against Manchester United and Everton, with the reverse of those games against our two biggest traditional rivals taking place on consecutive weekends in January.

The fixture list for the remainder of this year had already been locked in, and the first month of 2027 has now been set, other than prospective FA Cup and Carabao Cup matches.

On Thursday, the Premier League unveiled updated dates and times for matches in January, with two of Liverpool’s games being moved.

The home clash against Crystal Palace remains a 3pm kick-off on Saturday 16th, but the subsequent two games have unsurprisingly been chosen for TV coverage.

The Reds will now face Manchester United at Old Trafford on Sunday 24 January at 4:30pm (live on Sky Sports), with the Merseyside derby at Anfield taking place six days later with a 12:30pm kick-off (live on TNT Sports).

The newly introduced dates and times for the Man United and Everton games have left Liverpool with a rather difficult week towards the end of January.

Just three days after the game at Old Trafford, the Reds have their concluding fixture in the league phase of the Champions League at home to Lens, and then a turnaround of just over 50 hours to hosting the Toffees at Anfield.

*FA Cup third round draw and fixture details to be confirmed in December.

**If Liverpool advance to Carabao Cup semi-finals.

The hope is that, by the time the Ligue 1 outfit visit L4 on 27 January, we’ll already be assured of a direct passage to the round of 16 and there won’t be anything riding on that game for Andoni Iraola’s side.

Liverpool at the moment have seven matches in the diary in the first month of 2027, with an FA Cup third-round tie to be added for the weekend of 9/10 January and a potential Carabao Cup semi-final first leg in the subsequent midweek, should we defeat Bournemouth at Anfield next month.

It’s quite plausible that the Reds could have two matches against Everton in January, with both teams still in the Carabao Cup and favourites to win their respective quarter-finals (the Toffees are away to Fleetwood of League Two).

Three Merseyside derbies in the first five weeks of 2027 would be the definition of familiarity breeding contempt, but for now the sole focus for Iraola and co is the small matter of Man United at home on Sunday.
