Alisson Becker should continue in goal amidst reports of upcoming contract negotiations, shielded by a centre-back pairing of Virgil van Dijk and Jeremy Jacquet, who could be given more rest in the coming weeks with Giovanni Leoni returning to parts of team training this month.

Jeremie Frimpong was brought on as a substitute against United at the weekend, and could start at right-back on Wednesday, while Kostas Tsimikas comes in for Milos Kerkez at left-back.

Youngster Trey Nyoni has become a key part of Iraola's squad of late, and he is likely to line up alongside Alexis Mac Allister in the centre of the park, given that Ryan Gravenberch is a doubt due to a heel fracture and Dominik Szoboszlai recently recovered from a minor hamstring issue.

With Wirtz operating in the number 10 role, Victor Munoz and Bradley Barcola are the names in the frame out wide, with the latter hoping to find the back of the net after missing a number of chances against the Red Devils.

Cody Gakpo is a doubt after picking up a calf injury on international duty with the Netherlands, while 18-year-old Rio Ngumoha could begin the game on the bench for load management reasons, following his record-breaking goal and assist against Man United.

Alexander Isak has been in exceptional form this season, but he could be rotated in Brugge, leaving space for Lewis Koumas to lead the line on Wednesday.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ruben Amorim insisted that he and his AC Milan team are not getting carried away despite hammering Frosinone, and are simply focusing on the next game.

Milan were in a rampant mood tonight at San Siro, as they put five goals past Massimiliano Alvini’s side and it could have been more in truth. Goncalo Ramos, Ardon Jashari, Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic all scored, in addition to an own-goal that opened the scoring.

Industry observers note that read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It was crucial that the Rossoneri build on their victory over Genoa before the break, especially given that Lazio, Roma, Como and Juventus all won earlier in the round. In addition to that, several individuals shone and the team highlighted the levels that they are capable of.

Now, the challenge is to follow it up and get back on course in the Europa League in Greece on Thursday night. Amorim spoke to Sky after the final whistle to reflect on what was a very positive night for his side, with his words relayed by MilanNews.

Is that the best Milan performance since you have been here?

Industry observers note that “It’s a good feeling, but it’s not just the result: it’s also about consistency throughout the 90 minutes of the match, but now we’re thinking about the next one. It’s always like that at this club, always thinking about the next one.

“Tonight we played well, we were intelligent, courageous, and it showed towards the end of the match. We were tired, yet Frosinone continued to make transitions, but we managed to control them well.

“We could have even scored more goals. Perhaps in the middle of the first half we struggled a little and we need to improve in one-on-one situations defensively, but anyway, it was a good night for us tonight.”.

Are you happy for Gonçalo Ramos? How is he?

“We can’t lose any more players. All our players can play every game, but we have little time to recover for the Europa League, so we can’t risk anything. It was better to take him off.

It has been revealed that “I imagine he wasn’t happy, but I’m still happy for him, for his goal, especially for the 2-0. It was a goal that made the difference in a match against a team that is very strong in one-on-one transitions.”.

Is Rabiot one of the best you’ve ever coached?

Recent findings suggest that “I don’t want to say he could have had a better career because he played at PSG. Now he’s here at Milan and we want him to stay.

“Obviously, he’s a player who can play as a number 10, as an attacking midfielder, he can also play as a number 8, he can also play as a slightly deeper playmaker, even if he doesn’t like it.

“He’s definitely one of the best players I’ve ever coached, he’s one of the best midfielders in Europe right now.”.

What will you say ahead of Olympiacos?

Recent findings suggest that “The first thing I’ll say is that we have to win the match: if we don’t, then it will be really difficult to qualify for the next stage. Then I think that with Rabiot and Pulisic’s characteristics of playing between the lines, when they can’t play, we have to play and approach the game differently.

“But that’s not an excuse. I mentioned the same things against Ferencváros: we should have played a different game and gotten a different result, but what I’m trying to say is that if we don’t win the match, it will be really difficult and things will go badly for us.

“Then, if we exit the Europa League, we’ll only play once a week and many players won’t play enough. However, I think that if we stay in Europe, we can play more and everyone will continue to grow.

According to recent reports, “Furthermore, if we don’t qualify, we will fail to achieve an important objective: so that’s why we have to start the match differently than Benfica and Ferencváros. We’ll see.”.

What can you tell us about Cisse as a striker?

“I think he can play very well in that role, in that position. Tonight I chose Cissé to play in that position and not Camarda because against Frosinone, one-on-one, Cissé has these characteristics more. Tonight the goal wasn’t to keep possession, but to run and attack the space.

Recent findings suggest that “Cissé is better at this than Camarda. We wanted to make more transitions than Frosinone, so it was a choice dictated by the player’s characteristics, but I think Cissé is good both as an attacking midfielder and as a central striker, and not just as a winger.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Liverpool are reportedly showing ‘concrete interest’ in highly-rated Gladbach talent Wael Mohya.

The Bundesliga teenager is high up on the list at German giants Bayern Munich, with the Bavarians expected to face competition from Bayer Leverkusen for his signature.

The attacking midfielder has registered four goal contributions in 11 games (across all competitions) this season.

Christian Falk told CF Bayern Insider: “However, Bayern Munich definitely have him on the list. And we should note that both Liverpool and Brighton in the Premier League are showing concrete interest in the 17-year-old attacking talent.

“This is why Gladbach would be well-advised to try and offer him a new contract; that way, they can have some influence over how long the player stays at the club, or, at the very least, ensure that they get a sizeable sum from a permanent transfer.

It has been revealed that “I heard that there has already been contact with Mohya’s agent, Thies Bliemeister, and they talked about a move to Leverkusen. The next step is to talk to the player, his family and then the club. He doesn’t have a long-term contract at Gladbach, so there is a chance to make this deal happen.”.

With a contract currently set to expire in the summer of 2028, Mohya represents a genuine market opportunity for clubs looking to invest in a high-potential option.

On that note, Brighton makes a great deal of sense as the next stop in the 17-year-old’s career (if not his final destination), similarly to Leverkusen in the German top-flight.

Liverpool, it has to be noted, would benefit greatly from a player with the Gladbach star’s profile, given they lack a viable backup option to Florian Wirtz in the ten position. Not to mention the fact that the footballer would provide further reassurance on the flanks.

Recent findings suggest that falk went on to add: “The 17-year-old was invited to the national team by Klopp during the international break. He wasn’t officially part of the squad; it was more just to give the player a taste of what international football looks like. He’s not totally clear yet about where he wants to commit, but Germany is putting up a strong fight to ensure that he pledges his international future to Die Nationalelf.”.

The major concern facing Mohya in the coming weeks and months, of course, is whether a move to the likes of FC Bayern and Liverpool are actually in his best interest at this stage in his career.

Bayern Munich have Ismael Saibari and Jamal Musiala behind Harry Kane, albeit there are question marks over the latter’s long-term future in Munich in light of ongoing concerns over his health.

Sources indicate that the Reds, of course, have Wirtz, in whom they invested a British transfer record fee (the total package being worth £116.5m). He’s played a significant percentage of the total minutes on offer in 2026/27 under newly introduced boss Andoni Iraola, and at 23 years of age, he’s hardly at any risk of sinking past his peak in the near future.

We’ve no doubt Liverpool would welcome having a rotational option of Mohya’s quality, whom they could develop on their own time, and they can supply evidence of how well they’re managing Rio Ngumoha’s development despite the presence of more senior figures in Bradley Barcola and Cody Gakpo.

But if Wael Mohya’s looking for an absolute guarantee of regular minutes, you could forgive him for either staying put in Germany or joining the talent factory line in Brighton.

Former Liverpool defender Jamie Carragher has claimed Chelsea have "no chance of achieving anything" under Xabi Alonso unless they sign a physical centre-back.

Alonso has made an underwhelming start to his time at Stamford Bridge, having overseen five wins, one draw and five losses in the Premier League.

Chelsea's frailties in the defensive third have contributed to their inconsistency, having shipped 20 goals in 11 league games this term, leaving them with the fifth-worst defensive record in the top flight.

The Blues shipped four of those goals in Saturday's demoralising 4-1 defeat against Leeds United at Stamford Bridge.

Wesley Fofana and Levi Colwill started as Chelsea's centre-back pairing at the weekend, with Maxence Lacroix currently sidelined with a hamstring injury.

Speaking on Sky Sports' Monday Night Football, Carragher criticised Fofana and Colwill for their lack of physicality, telling Chelsea to address the centre-back position in the January transfer window.

"Chelsea have got a massive problem at centre-back, and if they don't change it in January, they're going to have a major problem in terms of where they feel they should be this season with the Champions League," Carragher noted.

"Colwill at Sunderland against Brobbey gave the penalty away, and the manager took him off at half-time.

"Fofana's performance against Man United, especially in the first half, was one of the worst you'll see from a centre-back this season.

"As a partnership, this will never work because they're not physical enough and there's no real leader there.

"It almost feels like you've got two novices playing, but one cost £75m, and Colwill has been talked up a lot not just at Chelsea but at international level as well.".

In a recent development, "Those two can't play in a back four as a two, but it reminds me of myself at Liverpool. We didn't fix it defensively and we were seen as weak, conceding from set pieces and long throws.

"It wasn't until we signed Sami Hyypia, 6ft 4in, dominant centre-back, leader, great player, that it changed for us.

In a recent development, "This is not going to change with what they have. Lacroix is a decent player, that's a sticking plaster until the next transfer window in January or the end of the season.

"Until they sign that dominant centre-back and leader, they've got absolutely no chance of achieving anything.".

After splashing out £52m on Lacroix in the summer, Chelsea may be somewhat reluctant to spend more money on their central defence in the January window.

However, if their defensive concerns persist, they may be forced into recruiting a new centre-back in a bid to add some much-needed solidity to Alonso's backline.

Recently, Chelsea have been mentioned as a potential suitor for AC Milan defender Koni De Winter, who has also been linked with Manchester United and Liverpool.

Chelsea are also said to be interested in Lens defender Pierre Ismael Ganiou, who has drawn comparisons with former Real Madrid centre-back Raphael Varane.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United are like John Toshack’s duvet. You fix one problem – being far too vulnerable to conceding goals – only to create another – lacking the threat to score. It is all very Meh United not Man United. The indisputable fact is they are just not very entertaining to watch. They are slow and dull.

In the end it also points to another thing. The thing highlighted in midweek by Lisandro Martínez after the Champions League defeat at Atlético Madrid: they do not have the strength in depth to compete.

It has been revealed that what they do have appears to not be fit for purpose. Certainly Michael Carrick, the under-pressure manager, is struggling to get the best out of the resources he has.

“It’s like a duvet,” Toshack, the former Real Madrid and Wales manager, famously mentioned of football. “If you pull it up, your feet get cold. If you pull it down, your shoulders get cold.”.

There will have been times in the last few days, with the intense criticism and scrutiny over his future, when Carrick will have simply felt like dragging that duvet up over his head and keeping it there.

Defeat by Leeds United would have been unthinkable. It would have put Carrick under potentially intolerable pressure in what appears to be a pivotal week, with Como away in the Champions League and a home Premier League fixture against Bournemouth in the coming days.

Recent findings suggest that was this a lifeline or the tightening of the noose for Carrick? Time will soon tell. The relief of avoiding defeat was tempered by the reality of it now being just one win in their opening seven league games – at home to newly promoted Ipswich Town – and they are down in 13th place. It is six games without a win in all competitions.

Recent findings suggest that that is unacceptable and is their fewest number of league victories in a top-flight campaign since 1986-87. Back then they sacked their manager in November and brought in a certain Alex Ferguson.

Sources indicate that the hard truth is Carrick needs to start collecting some “Ws” in those results columns. United are already 14 points behind leaders Manchester City and five outside the probable Champions League places. Qualifying again for that tournament must be the minimum expectation.

Ruben Amorim, Carrick’s predecessor, lost his job within 24 hours of the same 1-1 scoreline at Elland Road last season – dismissed after Martínez-like explosive comments again aimed at director of football Jason Wilcox. Carrick will not suffer the same fate after this, but the ice is becoming increasingly thin.

Sources indicate that we have seen this movie before at United. A slow start to the season, a period of drift, falling out of contention, no reaction on the pitch, backing from the hierarchy that becomes increasingly unconvincing. And then a change.

Recent findings suggest that can Carrick, who genuinely does still retain support at the highest level, alter that pattern? Does he have it in him? Is he too passive like his team? Carrick said this draw felt like a “fresh start”, but on this evidence that comment can be classified as wildly optimistic.

Having directed his criticism at the United hierarchy, and specifically Wilcox, the former Leeds winger who was here, over a lack of summer signings, Martínez apologised and was named in the starting XI. But the Argentine only lasted to half-time, withdrawn injured with a tight thigh, and sat watching the second half with his hood up over his head.

What United did sign in the last window was three midfielders – at a cost of £155m – and all three started: Carlos Baleba alongside Andrey Santos with Youri Tielemans in the No 10 role, which meant Bruno Fernandes was pushed out to the left, from where he constantly wanted to come in-field, with Amad Diallo on the right.

Carrick talked of having a “fresh spine” as well as that fresh start. But it did not make for a potent combination even if, further forward, Bryan Mbeumo played through the middle and scored one. He should have scored another.

Bryan Mbeumo finds the net this time to put Manchester United 1-0 up at Leeds! 🔴 https://t.co/NKDIhlUND1.

But beyond that United created little. “It was a dominant performance against Man United,” Daniel Farke, the Leeds manager, claimed. He was right. If one team deserved to win it was his. They had the chances but snatched at them with Anton Stach, in injury time, having a weak shot cleared off the line by Martínez’s replacement Noussair Mazraoui after a mistake by goalkeeper Senne Lammens. Stach had to score.

Recent findings suggest that united were ahead at half-time. Mbeumo had headed wastefully wide when unmarked but did well to force his way past James Justin and meet a low cross from Tielemans to poke the ball home. The way the usually undemonstrative Carrick punched the air in his technical area demonstrated the pressure he felt. It was something to build on. To gain control.

It has been revealed that leeds had started well but did not really pose much of a threat – beyond forcing Lammens to save well from Nico Elvedi’s downward header – and maybe the earlier kick-off subdued the crowd. This was far from a bear pit.

But after the break, Leeds were comfortably the better side. The nature of their equalising goal, with Dominic Calvert-Lewin too strong and alert for first Baleba and then Mbeumo to fire in from a corner, exposed the enduring softness at the heart of United.

Dominic Calvert-Lewin equalises for Leeds against Manchester United 👊 https://t.co/mnpyxZJKbm.

According to recent reports, and that must be addressed by Carrick, especially as he appeared to sacrifice attacking intent by shoring up defensively. But that duvet is looking far too inadequate right now. Or Carrick is making it appear so.

Michael Carrick says he has put on “the headphones” this week in an effort to drown out the noise, but admitted Manchester United have to stop their struggles from snowballing.

United sit just two points above the relegation zone after a 1-1 draw at Leeds left them with just one win from their opening seven Premier League matches.

Carrick claimed the result felt like a “fresh start” after a week in which Lisandro Martínez publicly apologised for criticising Jason Wilcox, the United director of football, and the Old Trafford board.

But the United manager acknowledged their position “doesn’t look too good” and that they must start winning soon to stop the club from entering another doom cycle.

“Listen, we’re not accepting it as everything’s great by any stretch, so I’m realistic with that,” said the United manager, who claimed “the headphones have been on this week”.

According to recent reports, “But sometimes you do struggle, sometimes there’s a bit of it where you have to find a way through it. We haven’t really had to go through that yet [before now] and we have to find a way through it.

Recent findings suggest that “There has been a cycle at times here over a period of time when it can go in different directions. We’ve got to be stable enough to keep doing the right things for the right reasons as a group, and we’re more than capable of winning football matches.

“I understand the situation doesn’t look too good if you look at it from a certain way, but I’ve no doubts we can go on a good run.”.

United face Como in the Champions League in Italy on Wednesday before Bournemouth visit Old Trafford four days later.

Sources indicate that carrick remarked he remains convinced United can still have a strong campaign, despite their worst start to a season for 40 years. I know what we’ve got in the changing room, where we want to get to, how we want to get there,” he said. “We know we can do it.

“We’ve done it for some time, and we feel we’re a better group now, and I do feel that. Sometimes it doesn’t always show, but you get a feeling and I’m encouraged by a lot of things. And if we keep doing the right things, I think we can still have a really good season.”.

Asked if he would be putting the headphones back on this week ahead of two more pivotal games, Carrick added: “Nah, it’s always quiet for me.”.

Industry observers note that martínez was substituted at half-time at Elland Road with a tight thigh just days after his tirade at club executives and Marcus Rashford was left out for “purely tactical” reasons. “Nothing personal, the front players were doing a good job on and off the ball,” Carrick noted. “Everyone is ready for Wednesday.”.

In a recent development, the Leeds boss told Sky Sports: “We are slightly disappointed it is just a point. Overall, I felt it was not necessary to be losing at half time but it is still Manchester United. Second half, we got the equaliser, we should have kept up the dominance, too many strikes went over the crossbar but it was overall a solid performance. We should have won the game but we move on.

It has been revealed that “We took it as a compliment that we have done many things right over the last month if we were seen as favourites against Manchester Untiedbut we have earned this. We wanted to prove the comments right.

“We were the dominant side but we couldn’t capitalise as we lacked quality in and around the box.

It has been revealed that “It says a lot about how much respect we have earned. Overall, this is where we are at the moment and overall, it is a good place to be.

Industry observers note that “It is still difficult in this league to win points. You have to be clinical and be very, very effective but we have to keep going.”.

Speaking to Sky Sports, he remarked: “I think we could’ve played with a bit more quality in the final third, particularly in the first half. We were getting good quality in the box but just not enough numbers.

Sources indicate that “We made sure in the second half we came out with more confidence going forward. I think we were unlucky not to win the game.

“They tried to [match us up formation-wise]. Not surprised given what happened last season. They were probably looking at our physical output and the way we liked to play and tried to go man-for-man.

“It took us a little bit to adjust to it, but I don’t think it was too difficult to adjust. It was more down to us and maybe a lack of quality in the final third.”.

Unconvincing goalkeeping from Lammens as he only punches Ampadu’s cross as far as Stach, whose tame shot squeezes through the Belgian’s legs. However, it’s blocked by the Man Utd defence and Lammens eventually gathers the ball.

Recent findings suggest that three times now United have looked like they’re about to get away down the flanks in the last few minutes and each time they’ve been flagged offside (Amad twice, Mbeumo once) and each occasion the player was able to look across the line. Carrick looked to the heavens. And he’s right to be frustrated. So avoidable.

Chris Sutton has mentioned he can ‘only see one result’ from Liverpool’s showdown against Manchester United at Anfield on Sunday afternoon.

The home side go into the fixture 10 points and 14 places ahead of their arch-rivals, for whom this is a first game in charge for newly introduced head coach Mauricio Pochettino.

The Reds’ home record in the Premier League so far this season has been poor, with just one win from five, but victory today would see them close to within one point of third-placed Manchester City.

In his weekly Premier League column for BBC Sport, Sutton voiced his belief that the visitors won’t have any ‘newly introduced manager bounce’ at Anfield and has forecast Liverpool to win handsomely.

The former Chelsea striker wrote: ‘Liverpool are still a work in progress, and United have picked up some results at Anfield recently – two draws and a win in their past three visits – but I can only see one result here, and it is a home victory.

Sources indicate that ‘Pochettino will probably look to defend and play on the counterattack, and they might get some chances that way, but Liverpool are going to win. The only question is how many they will score.

‘Carrick began by beating Manchester City and Arsenal in his first two games in January. Pochettino might start by being on the wrong end of a pummelling.’.

Sutton has predicted a resounding 4-0 win for Liverpool, matching the scoreline from this fixture in April 2022.

However, the pundit referenced Man United’s good record at Anfield since the famous 7-0 drubbing in March 2023, and Liverpool were also widely expected to win on a couple of those occasions.

Pochettino has never lost his first match at any of the five clubs he’s previously managed, and Reds fans might naturally be wary that the players who effectively downed tools under Michael Carrick will suddenly have a spring in their step today.

The good news for Iraola is that he has a mostly fully-fit squad, with Virgil van Dijk and Dominik Szoboszlai overcoming minor issues over the past couple of weeks and Ryan Gravenberch available once more, and there were no fresh injury casualties over the international window.

The Women's World Cup is coming home... but 2035 cannot be treated as a fix for the game's problems, writes TARA ANSON-WALSH

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The United Kingdom will host the 2035 Women's World Cup, the first football World Cup to be staged on these shores since 1966, it was announced to much fanfare on Monday.
  • Yet while the countdown can now officially begin, the biggest challenges facing the women's game cannot be kicked eight-and-a-half years down the road.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By TARA ANSON-WALSH, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 14:36 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 17:04 EST, 23 November 2026.

The United Kingdom will host the 2035 Women's World Cup, the first football World Cup to be staged on these shores since 1966, it was announced to much fanfare on Monday.

Yet while the countdown can now officially begin, the biggest challenges facing the women's game cannot be kicked eight-and-a-half years down the road.

Over in Zurich, FIFA president Gianni Infantino undertook his usual long-winded and self-serving monologue which precedes these ceremonies, in which he heralded the 'incredible growth' of the Women's World Cup, describing a time when they 'didn't exist'.

'We all remember the last Women's World Cup,' the embattled 56-year-old Italian said, calling it 'a huge success'.

The irony, of course, is that the last Women's World Cup in Australia and New Zealand is remembered by many for all the wrong reasons, with newspaper back pages peppered with images of Spain captain Jenni Hermoso's kiss with the former president of Spain's FA, Luis Rubiales, for days after the final.

Rubiales was later convicted of sexual assault for the incident, which triggered widespread protests across the country and overshadowed Spain's terrific 1-0 triumph over England in Sydney.

Gianni Infantino undertook his usual long-winded and self-serving monologue which precedes these ceremonies, in which he heralded the 'incredible growth' of the Women's World Cup.

Rubiales was later convicted of sexual assault for the incident, which triggered widespread protests across the country and overshadowed Spain's terrific 1-0 triumph over England.

There is an added layer of irony in that Infantino had, two days before the 2023 final, angered many women worldwide with yet another controversial speech in which he told them: 'You have the power to change', but that they had to 'convince us men what we have to do'.

Alongside this patronising statement, Infantino also insisted that equal pay at the World Cup 'would not solve anything'.

Three years later, Infantino is unfortunately still at the helm, while UEFA's attempts to unseat him following his controversial bid to sell off the World Cup now look to have failed spectacularly, with the football despot increasingly likely to secure a fourth term.

What the social and political landscape will look like by the time this women's footballing bonanza arrives on these shores in 2035 remains unclear. What is clear, however, is that the game's continued progress will require more than the record attendances and soaring commercial revenues the FA are predicting.

It will require the figures who have too often held it back to finally step aside, and that process should begin with the likes of Infantino being shown the door.

It has been revealed that it will require those at the top of English football to put their heads together and work out how to stem falling attendances in the league. The average attendance across the first eight WSL matchweeks of 2024-25 was 8,173. Last season it was 7,472. This season, it is tracking at around 5,677.

And third, it will require somewhere other than Wembley to stage the final.

Wembley was, of course, the scene of Chloe Kelly's moment of madness, yet by the time the 2035 Women's World Cup comes around it will also have hosted the men's finals of Euro 2024 and 2028.

The FA paid off its debt on the national stadium in 2024, 17 years after its reopening, and is no longer obligated to host major events there to service repayments.

The rules have been left open for another venue to emerge to host the final, such as Man United's proposed newly introduced 100,000 stadium.

While under current FIFA regulations, Wembley is the only one of the proposed 22 stadiums that meets the requirements to host a final, the rules have been left open enough for another venue to emerge should a suitable stadium be completed before 2035.

Step up Sir Jim Ratcliffe, although please refer back to point one in this regard – the Manchester United co-owner who famously asked former captain Katie Zelem 'what do you do here?' while touring the club's women's facilities.

United's proposed newly introduced 100,000-seater stadium was included in the 2035 bid and could yet come under consideration from FIFA.

While there are still many hurdles to clear before then, hosting a tournament final in Manchester would undoubtedly be huge for the women's game, not least given the optics of a bid built around being 'all together', described as 'a rallying cry to unite people through football'.

London should not be the epicentre of the tournament, not if the intention is to spread the women's game across the United Kingdom rather than concentrate it in the capital, where Arsenal's attendances continue to dwarf those of every other WSL club.

In other words, the women's game in this country cannot be put on hold until 2035.

It cannot afford to wait eight-and-a-half years for this World Cup to come and rescue it. Time to get cracking.

By Ben Sully | 24 Nov 2026 01:20, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 02:59.

Liverpool have reportedly started negotiations with goalkeeper Alisson Becker over a latest contract.

Alisson is just two games away from reaching an appearance milestone, having featured in 348 competitive matches since joining the Reds from Roma in the summer of 2028.

The Brazilian has been viewed as one of the world's best goalkeepers for the majority of his time at Anfield, and has helped the club win numerous honours, including two Premier League titles and the 2018-2019 Champions League.

Alisson has, unsurprisingly, remained the Reds' undisputed number one under Andoni Iraola, although there is some uncertainty about how much longer he will continue to be Liverpool's goalkeeper.

That is because his contract will expire at the end of the current campaign, which means Liverpool are at the moment running the risk of losing the experienced shot-stopper as a free agent.

According to Nicolo Schira, Liverpool are taking steps to address that glitch by opening talks with Alisson over a new deal.

The Brazil international is said to be open to extending his stay at Anfield until the end of the 2028-29 season.

Flamengo and Juventus were stated to be interested in signing Alisson in the summer transfer window, but Iraola and the Liverpool hierarchy made it clear he was 'non-transferable'.

AI is ditching hallucinated references — and other bad habits

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (793 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Hallucinated academic citations have become a hallmark of the artificial-intelligence era.
  • The finding is part of an analysis that reports that many LLM tendencies, such as overthinking simple mathematics problems and complying with illogical requests, fade over time as AI companies release fresh or updated models with improved capabilities.
  • “We, as users of these systems, need to not have such a fixed view of what AI can do and what it can’t do,” notes co-author Owen Queen, an AI researcher at Stanford University in California.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Credit: FabrikaSimf/Shutterstock.

Hallucinated academic citations have become a hallmark of the artificial-intelligence era. But they might soon be gone for good. Researchers have found that the latest large language models (LLMs) rarely, if ever, attribute information to sources that don’t exist.

The finding is part of an analysis that reports that many LLM tendencies, such as overthinking simple mathematics problems and complying with illogical requests, fade over time as AI companies release fresh or updated models with improved capabilities. Many of these tendencies disappear about 16 months after the phenomenon is first described in a published paper. The analysis, described in a blogpost, has not been peer reviewed.

“We, as users of these systems, need to not have such a fixed view of what AI can do and what it can’t do,” notes co-author Owen Queen, an AI researcher at Stanford University in California.

It has been revealed that but just because an LLM behaviour fades as models improve doesn’t mean that the effect immediately disappears, notes Maxim Topaz, a health-care AI researcher at Columbia University in New York City. Topaz has found1 that the number of hallucinated citations in academic papers has risen drastically since 2023, probably because more researchers than ever before are using LLMs, and they often aren’t using the latest models.

It has been revealed that queen and his colleague identified 50 widely cited LLM behaviours that were described in publications between late 2022, when some of the first LLMs became widely available, and late 2025. They then gave the same prompts that first elicited the behaviour in the original publications to 20 LLMs that were released from mid-2024 to late 2026 to see if the effect has strengthened or weakened over time. For example, they asked each model to count the number of r’s in ‘strawberry’ — something that LLMs have found difficult but can now do more reliably.

It has been revealed that nearly half of the behaviours they checked have largely disappeared from newer models, leading the researchers to deem those effects ‘expired’. Expired behaviours had an average lifespan of about 16 months after publication, although some were fleeting — models stopped overthinking simple maths problems just a month and a half after this tendency was published. Other traits persisted, such as the stereotyping of Black women by disproportionately describing them as resilient, which lasted for longer than three years.

It has been revealed that although most of the retested LLM behaviours have faded over time, three have become more pronounced. Today’s models praise what their users like even more often than they used to, LLMs favour their own writing more strongly than that of other LLMs and people; and LLMs are now even worse than they used to be at generating truly random numbers.

doi: https://doi.org/10.1038/d41586-026-03753-1.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester City's owners already have $1billion (£764million) worth of "existing debt" before sealing upcoming loans.

That is according to former Man City financial adviser Stefan Borson, who exclusively told Football Insider that football clubs are "rarely profitable", and that is no different for the City Football Group.

The Citizens were understood to be one of the most well-run clubs in world football, at least until news of their 114 charges was brought to the forefront.

Now, Man City are facing a huge battle against the Premier League, potentially to actually remain in the division after countless broken rules.

It emerged that, due to the independent commission's findings, Apollo Global Management pulled out of loaning $2bn (£1.5bn) to Man City's owners.

Questions have been asked about what that money might have been used for, and the answer isn't nearly as exciting as many may have predicted.

Speaking exclusively to Football Insider, Borson has predicted what City Football Group's current finances look like, and why the loan was needed.

"Obviously, we're waiting for the latest set of numbers. So, it may be higher, but if you use, for the sake of simple numbers..." he stated.

"...Let's say $1bn (£764m) of existing debt. And then on top of that, they would raise, effectively, another $1bn. None of the companies are profitable, because football clubs are very rarely profitable.

"I don't think you should see it as simply that they needed $1bn for Manchester City.

"This was $2bn (£1.5bn) to refinance what's there already, with a bit left over for the running costs of the football group.".

Undoubtedly, £764m looks like a lot of debt, but the Man City owners know exactly what they're doing, not just at the Etihad, but across the CFG.

Manchester United's owners, on the other hand, are staring down the barrel of £1.15bn of debt, including historic borrowing, revolving credit facility and oustandings transfer fees.

The Glazers and INEOS are under tremendous pressure at Old Trafford, with jokes already being made about both clubs playing Championship football next season.

As Borson has explained, it's almost impossible not to be in debt as an owner in the Premier League, but some are better at running a business, that's for sure.

Mauricio Pochettino continues to rage over decisions which he feels went against his team in the 4-0 drubbing by Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday.

Industry observers note that manchester United were reduced to 10 men inside seven minutes when Leny Yoro barged into Alexander Isak and was adjudged to have denied a clear goalscoring opportunity. The red card has since been overturned on the basis that the Reds striker was unlikely to get to the ball had he not been impeded.

Dominik Szoboszlai opened the scoring from the resulting free kick, although the Red Devils head coach complained that Bradley Barcola was interfering with the visitors’ defensive wall from the set piece.

Sources indicate that speaking to the media ahead of Man United’s Champions League clash against Sporting Lisbon, Pochettino raged (via Liverpool Echo): “No-one talked about that the goal wasn’t legal. They should disallow the goal because Barcola was touching our wall.

It has been revealed that “[Eberechi] Eze, last season for Palace [against Chelsea], when Eze scored, [it was disallowed]. Why didn’t they check the VAR, check the goal? That must be disallowed.

“[I] need to defend my players and my club. Where are the three points? We need to think a little more deep in the way that we use the technology.”.

In a recent development, want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

While Pochettino might feel vindicated over his grievances about Yoro’s red card now that the decision has been overturned on appeal, he’s clutching at straws by complaining about the free kick from which Szoboszlai scored.

Replays show that it was actually Fernandes who pushed Barcola out of the way when the ball was struck, and the Liverpool forward most certainly isn’t at fault for how poorly the Man United defensive wall was set up.

Bruno literally pushed Barcola into the wall 😂😂😂😂 these lot are losing the plot.pic.twitter.com/tjPFU56OTg https://t.co/bJWXQfmfUk.

— LB (@LBLFC_) November 24, 2026.

Even though his team were very much discommoded by the early red card, their response to that setback was still a meek surrender, and that’s what should concern their head coach the most rather than blaming opposition players.

The Red Devils still had more than 80 minutes to reorganise and try to get a result, and while they did stem the tide for a large chunk of the game at 2-0, they were still indebted to wasteful finishing from the home side that the final score wasn’t even more emphatic.

While Pochettino moans, Liverpool will be busy preparing for their own Champions League clash away to Club Brugge, followed by the small matter of the Merseyside derby on Sunday.

  • Julian Schuster's side sit third in the Bundesliga and have not lost a home European fixture since West Ham United won at the Europa-Park Stadion in October 2023, a run of 13 straight home victories across the Europa League and Conference League, while John van den Brom's Twente arrive full of confidence after three straight wins in this season's Conference League campaign and a thrilling, see-saw run of Eredivisie results.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Nsidibe Akpan | 24 Nov 2026 06:41, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 20:45.

SC Freiburg host FC Twente at the Europa-Park Stadion on Thursday in matchday four of the UEFA Europa Conference League league phase.

Julian Schuster's side sit third in the Bundesliga and have not lost a home European fixture since West Ham United won at the Europa-Park Stadion in October 2023, a run of 13 straight home victories across the Europa League and Conference League, while John van den Brom's Twente arrive full of confidence after three straight wins in this season's Conference League campaign and a thrilling, see-saw run of Eredivisie results.

Freiburg moved level on points with Bayern Munich in the race for a Bundesliga top-three finish when Igor Matanovic's 68th-minute strike settled a 1-0 win at newly promoted Elversberg on November 21, a result that left Schuster's side third, two points behind leaders Borussia Dortmund.

Philipp Lienhart's long ball forced the error that led to the goal, and Jan-Niklas Beste pounced to square the ball for Matanovic, who picked out the bottom-right corner for his fifth Bundesliga goal of the season.

That result was Freiburg's third straight Bundesliga win, and it left them on 22 points from 10 matches, with a plus-11 goal difference bettered only by Bayern and RB Leipzig.

In the Conference League itself, Freiburg sit 14th of 36 teams with six points from three matchdays, beating Jablonec 3-2 at home on October 15 and winning 1-0 away at Trabzonspor on November 5, either side of a 3-0 defeat at Monaco on October 22.

The win at Trabzonspor ended home side Thomas Reis's winning run and kept a lid on Mohamed Salah, who had moved to the Turkish club over the summer, and Freiburg have also reached the DFB-Pokal's last 16 with wins over Fortuna Dusseldorf and Wolfsburg as they juggle three competitions at once.

Freiburg reached their first European final last season, losing 3-0 to Aston Villa in the Europa League final in Istanbul despite finishing only seventh in the Bundesliga, and they needed a 7-2 aggregate playoff win over Motherwell just to reach this season's Conference League.

Matanovic leads Freiburg's scoring this season, and two of the players around him, Derry Scherhant and Philipp Treu, have broken into Germany's senior squad under head coach Jurgen Klopp in recent months, a sign of the individual quality Schuster now has to call on.

Twente travel to Germany with a perfect record in this season's Conference League, beating Thun, Lincoln Red Imps and Pafos in their three league-phase matches to date, having reached the league phase at all only after dropping out of Europa League qualifying to Ferencvaros and then winning Conference League qualifying ties against Qarabag and Dundee United.

The 4-1 win at Lincoln Red Imps on October 22 and the 3-1 victory over Pafos at De Grolsch Veste on November 5 came either side of a 9-0 demolition of Excelsior in the Eredivisie on November 1, in which Wout Weghorst scored four.

Weghorst, a former Bundesliga forward at Wolfsburg and Hoffenheim who joined Twente on a free transfer from Ajax in the summer, has now scored nine Eredivisie goals from his first 12 appearances of the season, with the ninth coming via a stoppage-time penalty that rescued a 2-2 draw against his former club on November 8.

Twente had trailed that game 2-0 inside the opening hour before a Dies Janse own goal and Weghorst's 95th-minute spot kick, awarded after a VAR review for a foul on Ramiz Zerrouki, salvaged a point in chaotic scenes at De Grolsch Veste.

Norwegian winger Sondre Orjasaeter has been just as notable to Van den Brom's attack, registering seven Eredivisie assists to go with two goals of his own this season.

Twente then beat bottom club Willem II 2-1 at home on November 22, overturning Devin Haen's surprise 53rd-minute opener through a Zerrouki equaliser and a Marko Pjaca header with eight minutes to go, against a Willem II side reduced to 10 men before half time when Nathan Tjoe-A-On was shown a second yellow card for a foul on Daan Rots.

Freiburg Conference League form:.

FC Twente form (all competitions):.

Philipp Lienhart played the full 90 minutes at Elversberg and set up the winning goal, though he picked up a yellow card late on for a foul and will be assessed after a heavy workload across three competitions this month.

Derry Scherhant and Jan-Niklas Beste have both come off the bench to create goals in recent weeks, Scherhant teeing up Yuito Suzuki against Union Berlin and Beste setting up Matanovic in Elversberg, giving Schuster attacking options in reserve even when his starting front line is not firing.

For the visitors, Lars Unnerstall has not held the goalkeeper's jersey unchallenged all season, with close season arrival Joel Drommel deputising when Unnerstall was short of fitness for the draw at Fortuna Sittard on October 10.

Van den Brom has shuffled his frontline between Weghorst, Younes Taha and substitute Marko Pjaca in recent weeks, and the manager will have a selection call to make over who partners Weghorst after Pjaca's matchwinning intervention from the bench against Willem II.

Freiburg possible starting lineup:.

Backhaus; Kubler, Ginter, Lienhart, Makengo; Eggestein, Engelhardt; Beste, Suzuki, Scherhant; Matanovic.

FC Twente possible starting lineup:.

Drommel; Van Rooij, Propper, Nijstad, Adelgaard; Weidmann, Zerrouki, Rots; Orjasaeter, Taha, Weghorst.

Freiburg's run of 13 straight home wins in Europe, allied to Matanovic's five Bundesliga goals and the service he is getting from Scherhant and Beste, should be enough to see off a Twente side still finding their feet away from De Grolsch Veste.

Weghorst's record of nine Eredivisie goals in his first 12 appearances of the season makes him too dangerous to ignore completely, and on the evidence of his stoppage-time penalty against Ajax, a goal for the Dutchman feels likely even if Twente leave Germany empty-handed.

Everton will be resistant to making a big move for Cagliari striker Paul Mendy in January, sources have told Football Insider.

The 19-year-old has been linked with a surprise move to the Toffees, but it is understood that they view him as more of a long-term target at the moment.

Mendy only broke into the Cagliari team back in February, and is deemed to be a more cost-effective solution than some of Everton's other targets.

However, sources say that the club feel it would be "too substantial a gamble" to pin their hopes on Mendy in the second half of the season.

The Merseysiders feel that Mendy has a massive future ahead of him, but would prefer to add someone who is more "tried and tested" this winter.

Mendy has struck one goal and two assists from 12 games in Serie A so far this term, and is likely to continue developing with Cagliari for now.

Mendy has enjoyed a breakthrough six months with Cagliari, and it has grown his reputation beyond the confines of Serie A.

He won his first senior caps for Senegal in November, and netted his first international goal with a late strike against Sudan in AFCON qualifying.

Everton have identified Mendy as a striker who could have a huge future ahead of him at the top level, but they have a limited sample size in terms of what they have seen from him so far.

David Moyes' side are desperate to bring in support for Thierno Barry at the top of the pitch, but Mendy is being seen as a step too far at the moment.

It would be a big step up for him to immediately perform in the Premier League, but that will not stop Everton from paying close attention to his progress across the next 12 months.

Former Everton chief executive Keith Wyness told Football Insider on Wednesday that the Toffees' Hill Dickinson Stadium is a "shoo-in" to host the Nations League finals if the FA can win the rights.

The FA have already made their interest in hosting the event clear, should England get past Norway in the quarter-finals in March.

Wyness believes that the Hill Dickinson is the obvious choice to host the event, given that Wembley is already being used and the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium is understood to not be preferrable for the FA.

The FA are currently battling against rival nations for the hosting rights, but should they win out, then the event could be on Merseyside from 9 June until 13 June next summer.

Mauricio Pochettino has been handed a 'limited' winter transfer budget as he looks to turn Manchester United's season around with reinforcements.

The new Red Devils boss is expected to have the funds for just two January signings, despite several areas of his squad requiring attention.

United's financial restrictions could therefore leave the Argentine facing some difficult decisions when the transfer window opens.

According to the Daily Mail, Pochettino will have less than £50m to spend in January, with United's financial position and the Premier League's new financial rules restricting their spending power.

The former Tottenham Hotspur boss admitted that United are in a relegation battle after beginning his tenure with a painful 4-0 defeat to Liverpool at Anfield, leaving the club second from bottom.

The expectation is that Pochettino will be able to make two additions, potentially including a loan signing, although sources have not completely ruled out United gambling on further investment if their relegation threat becomes more serious.

Recent findings suggest that central defence is an obvious priority following the Anfield defeat, with Brentford's Nathan Collins emerging as a strong candidate. Calvin Bassey is another option, although he is expected to sign a fresh Fulham contract, while Everton's Jarrad Branthwaite is valued at more than £70m.

United are also interested in strengthening at left-back, having previously been linked with Barcelona's Alejandro Balde and Manchester City's Rayan Ait-Nouri.

It has been revealed that A striker is another consideration, particularly with Benjamin Sesko sidelined by a shin injury. However, Ivan Toney's reported £500,000-a-week wages make him an unrealistic option, while Leeds United are keen to extend Dominic Calvert-Lewin's £180,000-a-week contract.

A budget below £50m, alongside the expectation of only two additions, makes it difficult to see United addressing all three areas in January.

A move for someone like Lewis Hall at left-back or Branthwaite at centre-back would seemingly be beyond their financial reach, particularly if Newcastle and Everton demand substantial fees.

However, Balde and RB Leipzig's David Raum could represent more budget-friendly alternatives, depending on their respective clubs' willingness to negotiate.

Sources indicate that the bigger question is whether United can afford to strengthen centrally and up front as well. Collins could be a realistic defensive target, but finding the funds for another centre-back and a striker on top of that looks particularly difficult at this stage.

Unless United generate significant funds through player sales, Pochettino may have to prioritise two positions and make the best of the squad he inherits.

That is a worrying prospect for a behemoth of a club currently fighting to avoid relegation.

Industry observers note that within 20 minutes, the Rossoneri had already blown the game wide open, eventually putting five past their opponents. All of them were spectacular, lightning-fast, and following the same pattern: every single one a counter-attack.

In a recent development, it was a throwback style of football, yet infused with the visionary approach of Amorim, making it both fresh and truly beautiful to watch. There may not be official statistics on this, but conceding from five lethal transitions feels like a record as Frosinone’s strategy certainly went beyond mere self-sabotage.

Recent findings suggest that yet, on days like this, this Milan – an enigma to its opponents, with fluid movement and interchangeable positioning – are a truly daunting prospect. When Adrien Rabiot, Diego Moreira, Luka Modrić and others perform at such a high level, we see the potential of this side.

According to recent reports, the Diavolo have secured five wins in their last six league matches, yet in Europe, they have suffered three defeats in four games. Will Thursday’s clash against Olympiacos help restore the balance?

There was nothing balanced about the game between Milan and Frosinone. It is true that Alvini’s incredibly bold (perhaps even reckless) side tried to go toe-to-toe with their opponents for an hour by attacking, playing long balls, and taking on defenders.

Yet, beyond this emphasis on a specific style of play, one could make more concrete assessments. The coach clearly understood how vital Raimondo is to a team featuring such direct and creative wingers, Ghedjemis on the right and Kvernadze (who was rather ineffective yesterday) on the left.

Industry observers note that raimondo was the perfect focal point for them and without him, things had already gone poorly against Cagliari. Alvini attempted to make adjustments but got it wrong: he abandoned his 4-2-3-1 formation in favour of a back three (Calvani, Monterisi, Cittadini).

All this was undermined by a senseless tendency to push too high, maintaining a defensive line 57 metres from their own goal within a 3-4-3 setup that lacked a true striker, opting instead for a ‘false’ one in Schmid. Every time they lost possession, it resulted in a counter-attack and often a goal.

It has been revealed that it might seem odd to start with Frosinone rather than the brilliance of Milan, but there’s no denying that the visitors played their part in the spectacle. This is a match that future opponents will need to study in minute detail, because Milan on the counter are a goal-scoring machine.

Recent findings suggest that amorim, too, has a knack for springing surprises, though as always the guessing game regarding his actual tactical setup for the day begins the moment the whistle blows. For example, it was not a back four as it appeared on paper.

Instead, the system actually gradually morphed into a 3-5-2, with Rabiot operating as a highly advanced right-sided central midfielder, almost an attacking midfielder. The key lies in the connection between the Frenchman and the stratospheric Moreira, who surged down the centre often.

Sources indicate that keeping everything running at full throttle was the incredible playmaking of Modrić, who also serves as the team’s primary ball-winner. So much for being a ‘pensioner’.

Milan proved flawless in exploiting both structural weaknesses and individual errors. Frosinone’s DNA is defined by a headlong, aggressive approach, but the opening goal – stemming from a sequence on the right flank involving Modrić and Rabiot – ended up as an own goal by Calvani.

According to recent reports, just four minutes in, and the match was effectively decided. While Frosinone usually thrive on quick, darting attacks, here the roles were reversed. Another full-pitch surge, initiated by Ramos winning the ball from Calvani and carried forward by Moreira and Rabiot, left the Portuguese player unmarked to make it 2-0.

Recent findings suggest that only a reckless back pass from Musah gifted Masini a goal to pull it back to 2-1. In the second half, however, Amorim addressed the one area that looked shaky: he withdrew Bartesaghi – who had been struggling against Ghedjemis – shifting Musah to full-back and pairing Jashari with Modrić.

It paid off immediately: Jashari broke away and fired home the 3-1 following yet another rapid transition. And that wasn’t the only one: Pulisic surged clear on his own after a Frosinone corner (4-1), and Cissé, having just come on, joined the fray at full throttle to add the fifth (5-1).

Sources indicate that there were many top performances. Rabiot is like a freight train and deserved a goal. He had to settle for three assists (bringing his total to seven). Moreira is versatile, playing as a wing-back, a central midfielder, or a winger, much like he did for Belgium when they caused Italy so much trouble.

Sources indicate that ramos also moved well outside of his goal. Cissé was an absolute handful: he came on and scorrd, playing as a striker after the Portuguese felt a tweak. He did so with an effortless grace that makes him impossible for his markers to handle.

It has been revealed that the end result is that Milan are back in fourth. The competition is fierce, but the Rossoneri are right there in the mix, and eventually, some of the others will stumble. Take Inter, for example. Frosinone need to rethink their strategy while waiting for the return of Raimondo.

Sources indicate that they’ve overachieved so far, but now they might need to be a bit more prudent. And what about Milan? If they don’t turn their trip to Athens into a Greek tragedy, perhaps their European campaign can get back on track, too.

Latest Update: Sore throat? The brain has surprising control over how ill you feel

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that researchers are beginning to show how neurons in the brain detect an infection and tailor physiological responses to fight it.Credit: Dr.
  • A viral cold or bacterial infection can leave you feeling miserable, but each infection produces its own mix of symptoms.
  • Sources indicate that the findings, many of which are unpublished, were presented on 15 November at the Society for Neuroscience annual meeting in Washington DC, and challenge the established view of what it means to feel unwell.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that researchers are beginning to show how neurons in the brain detect an infection and tailor physiological responses to fight it.Credit: Dr. Chris Henstridge/SPL.

A viral cold or bacterial infection can leave you feeling miserable, but each infection produces its own mix of symptoms. Now, neuroscientists are discovering that the brain is the conductor of these responses — decoding the type of pathogen that has invaded, accessing memories of past bouts of illness and even mobilizing immune defences at the sight of a sick person.

Sources indicate that the findings, many of which are unpublished, were presented on 15 November at the Society for Neuroscience annual meeting in Washington DC, and challenge the established view of what it means to feel unwell. Neuroscientists have long viewed neurological responses to infection as a one-size-fits-all response to inflammation, rather than a strategy tailored to the threat.

“Sickness is actually not a fixed program, although we often talk about it this way,” said Jessica Osterhout, a neurobiologist at the University of Utah in Salt Lake City, who chaired the session.

Recent findings suggest that A bacterial infection and a cold caused by a virus can both result in fever and exhaustion, yet they rarely trigger the same constellation of symptoms. Bacterial infections, for instance, tend to suppress appetite much more sharply than do colds, which made Osterhout and her colleagues wonder how the brain tells various pathogens apart.

Your brain could be controlling how sick you get — and how you recover.

Your brain could be controlling how sick you get — and how you recover.

Sources indicate that in unpublished experiments, Osterhout’s team compared mice injected with a bacterial toxin with those given a compound that mimics a viral infection. To see how the brain distinguished between pathogens, the researchers profiled individual cells in circumventricular organs, which are specialized structures with unusually permeable blood vessels that surround brain ventricles.

When the body has an infection, cells in the circumventricular organs switch on sets of immune-related genes and release distinct mixes of chemical signals. Those signals diffuse to nearby neurons and create distinct patterns of activity for different pathogens, allowing the brain to customize its symptom profile depending on the threat.

Rather than acting as conduits that let inflammatory signals pass unchecked from the blood into the wider brain, these structures “may actually interpret them”, Osterhout said.

Sometimes, the brain doesn’t even wait for pathogens to enter the body to rally the immune system1. Andrea Serino, a neuroscientist at Lausanne University Hospital in Switzerland, studies how the brain maps peripersonal space, which is the area around the body roughly in arm’s reach.

When Serino’s team placed volunteers in virtual reality, they found that threat-monitoring brain regions became active when avatars bearing skin lesions caused by viral or bacterial infections approached, even when the figures were beyond arm’s reach. Just 15 minutes of virtual exposure triggered a surge in frontline immune ‘sentinel’ cells in participants’ blood comparable to that induced by an influenza vaccine. This reaction did not occur when participants saw healthy-looking avatars or ones expressing fear.

These experiments suggest that the immune system uses “the predictive ability of the brain to react before pathogens enter the body”, Serino said.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Andoni Iraola has mentioned that he thoroughly enjoyed his analysis of Club Brugge ahead of Liverpool’s Champions League fixture against the Belgian outfit tonight.

It’s the first time in 48 years that the teams have faced each other, with all three of their previous meetings coming in European finals – the two-legged 1976 UEFA Cup showpiece and the European Cup decider two years later (both of which the Reds won).

The sides have near-identical records going into the game at the Jan Breydel Stadium, with both on nine points and a +4 goal difference, and victory for either could catapult them into the top four of the league phase standings.

Speaking in his pre-match press conference on Tuesday, Iraola was notaly effusive in his praise of Club Brugge and is expecting a highly entertaining spectacle in Belgium.

It has been revealed that the Liverpool head coach noted (via liverpoolfc.com): “It’s not that they surprised me. I knew they were very good, but honestly I’ve enjoyed analysing them. Sometimes you have to analyse a team, you have to watch a lot of games and it’s a little bit boring!

It has been revealed that “With Brugge that definitely hasn’t happened. They are a very attractive team. They are very energetic, everyone runs, very aggressive in the press. They are coming with an incredible run of games. I think it’s 10 wins and a draw in the last 11. Also massive, big games in those – Inter Milan, PSV away.

(Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images).

“I think we will have to be at a very, very good level otherwise it’s going to be very difficult. They have players that can make the difference.

“I expect quite an open game because they are aggressive and we are aggressive. We want to press; they want to press. Probably there will be spaces in the game and I hope we can win those one-v-ones, individual battles that definitely tomorrow we are going to see, yes.”.

According to recent reports, want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

This might seem like classic pre-match diplomacy on Iraola’s part, but Club Brugge’s numbers from this season indicate that the Basque’s praise is very much justified.

Ivan Leko’s side have scored 45 goals in their 18 matches so far this term (2.5 per game), including 11 in their four Champions League outings (2.75 per game), including a memorable 4-3 triumph away to Inter Milan (who Liverpool will face at San Siro in January).

They’re scored three or more goals in seven of their 12 league matches in 2026/27, an impressive return even allowing for the quality of opposition in the Belgian top flight, and they’ve one forward who’s responsible for just over a third of their goals in the current campaign.

(Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images).

Nicolo Tresoldi has 16 goals from 18 games, including a hat-trick in the aforementioned win against Inter, and his last five league outings have seen him score seven times (Transfermarkt).

Club Brugge will be aware that Liverpool’s concession record in the Champions League this term has been pitiful, with 10 goals shipped across their four matches and three each in the games against LASK, Villarreal and Fenerbahce.

It has been revealed that iraola may have enjoyed analysing tonight’s opponents over the past few days, but he won’t be too enamoured if they put the Reds to the sword in Belgium. The Merseysiders can’t say they haven’t been forewarned.

Newly introduced boss Scott Parker is keen to make several changes to the squad at the London Stadium, with the team slowly falling away from the promotion race in the Championship.

Parker has already made his desire for an overhaul clear to the recruitment team, who are assembling a list of targets ahead of the window.

Sources say that the boss feels that the addition of a "proven goalscorer" is a necessity if West Ham are to get back to the Premier League at the first attempt.

The upcoming boss remains winless after his opening four games in charge, and the East London outfit are now sitting in 12th.

They have promptly fallen 10 points adrift of the automatic promotion places, and know that they must get January right to get back into contention.

West Ham are the Championship's leading goalscorers so far this term, but their tally of 38 league strikes has been inflated somewhat.

Their pair of 6-0 victories over Wrexham and Lincoln City have helped to inflate that figure a little, and perhaps hide some of the complications that have been brewing.

Despite the Hammers' lofty goal tally, just six of their strikes have come from their recognised strikers.

Taty Castellanos and Pablo both have one goal apiece, while Joel Piroe is not faring much better on four.

That is a situation that Parker is hoping to see rectified in January, given the sustained challenges that the trio are experiencing.

However, West Ham are also aware that goalscoring strikers often come at a premium in the middle of a campaign.

Football Insider revealed on Tuesday that West Ham feel that selling Castellanos in January is a move that will "suit all parties.".

The Argentine has made it clear that he is keen to leave the club, and West Ham have been hugely disappointed with his performances since their relegation.

The Hammers are prepared to sell the 28-year-old at a loss, knowng that it will be "very difficult" for them to recoup the £26million they paid for him last January.

Castellanos netted six Premier League goals from just 18 games last term, but he has struggled to find any sort of form so far in 2026-27.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Lewis Blain | 24 Nov 2026 07:16.

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta has warned Ethan Nwaneri that brief flashes of quality will not be enough to secure regular football at Borussia Dortmund.

The record-breaking 19-year-old joined the Bundesliga leaders on loan from the Gunners in the summer, but has struggled for opportunities in recent weeks.

Nwaneri could now face his parent club in Tuesday's Champions League meeting in north London, with Arteta making his expectations clear.

Nwaneri initially enjoyed opportunities in Niko Kovac's starting lineup after arriving in Germany, but his involvement has since diminished significantly.

The versatile attacking midfielder has not started a match in over a month and has played just five minutes across Dortmund's last three Bundesliga fixtures.

Arteta believes the teenager must show greater consistency to establish himself at the highest level, insisting that occasional impressive performances are not enough.

It has been revealed that "We're talking here about the highest level in Europe," the Arsenal boss noted (via the Evening Standard). "You can just shine in moments, but moments are not enough. Now you need to show the consistency.".

The Spaniard also stressed that Nwaneri must earn his place in a talented Dortmund squad, rather than expect opportunities because of his Arsenal background.

"He needs to earn the right to play," Arteta added, explaining that joining a major European club does not automatically guarantee minutes.

Arteta remains convinced that Nwaneri has the mentality and quality to succeed, but acknowledged that his loan spells at Marseille and Dortmund form part of a challenging development journey.

Arsenal are understood to have the option to recall the youngster in January if his situation does not improve, with Arteta currently unconvinced that the Dortmund move is delivering the desired benefits.

Nwaneri is eligible to feature against his parent club on Tuesday, although Dortmund's strong form makes a starting place appear unlikely.

Nevertheless, the opportunity to face Arsenal off the bench could provide the teenager with an ideal platform to respond to Arteta's comments, particularly after his recent lack of involvement.

It has been revealed that the Gunners boss has challenged him to show consistency and earn his place, rather than rely on occasional moments of quality. A positive contribution against the Premier League champions would certainly help his case.

Should Nwaneri find the net, he could join a select group of players to score against their parent clubs while on loan, including James Rodriguez against Real Madrid and Philippe Coutinho against Barcelona during their respective spells at Bayern Munich.

It would be a significant way to make his mark, although simply earning meaningful minutes against Arsenal would represent an encouraging step in his Dortmund journey.

Alphadjo Cisse has revealed that he would like to add more assists to his game, as well as why he has Matteo Gabbia to thank above all.

Milan put on a ruthless display at San Siro on Sunday night, beating Frosinone 5-1 to move back into the top four. Calvani’s own-goal started the rout, while Goncalo Ramos, Ardon Jashari and Christian Pulisic all scored.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Sources indicate that cisse got his name on the scoresheet again just minutes after coming on, netting his ninth goal of the season. Diego Moreira set him up with a nice through ball in transition, and though the offside flag went up initially, VAR overturned it to award the goal.

In a recent development, after the game, Cisse spoke to both Sky and DAZN to give his thoughts on what was another very positive night for him personally and for the team. His comments are via MilanNews.

What position do you prefer to play?

Recent findings suggest that “I definitely always try to contribute in all positions, and I definitely prefer to play in my own position, but I’m always available in all roles. Which position? I won’t say (laughs).”.

Where can you still grow and what does Amorim ask of you?

According to recent reports, “I have to improve in many other areas. As always, scoring is always great. I’d also like to add a few assists for some of my team-mates, but the most crucial thing was always to bring home three points, and today we did that.”.

Is there a team-mate you have to thank in particular?

In a recent development, “I definitely think Gabbia, because I was initially coming from Serie B, and settling into that kind of environment is never easy. But I had teammates who welcomed me very well, him especially, so for me everything was much easier.”.

We also see you as a possible centre-forward….

Industry observers note that “I’ll tell you the truth, come on, I’ll tell you. I prefer to play in the attacking midfield because, as I’ve always done, I always want to try to make plays, to entertain people. But maybe, who knows, I’ll also play as a striker, I don’t know. Let’s see…”.

Did you know you weren’t offside?

“At first I thought it was. Then, as they were checking it a bit, I thought it wasn’t.”.

According to recent reports, you’re Milan’s top scorer. Will we see a bicycle kick soon?

“The overhead kick used to be my specialty, but now it’s not. Let’s hope it happens. It’s always a great feeling to score, I want to add a few assists too. The important thing was the three points, and we got them.”.

How far along are you in your development?

“Right now, I’m not even halfway there. Maybe even lower. There’s still a lot of work to do to get there. But I’m in the right place, and hopefully we can get there.”.

Have you ever thought about what would have happened if you had gone to PSV?

It has been revealed that “Better not to think about it. Let’s just say that I’ve always made the right decisions with my family, and thanks go to them, to the coach, to my team-mates, and I’m in the right place and on the right path.”.

How much is Amorim protecting you?

“Progress is the right word, because we’ve changed coaches, and it’s never easy. We’re a great team, with many champions. We still have a lot of work to do. Milan always has our backs, and that’s very notable to me.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Lewis Blain | 24 Nov 2026 07:38.

Chelsea have decided against making an immediate change in the dugout despite growing pressure on manager Xabi Alonso.

The Blues have won just one of their last five matches, with a 4-1 defeat to Leeds United at Stamford Bridge only intensifying scrutiny of the Spaniard.

However, the club hierarchy are understood to remain keen to give their summer appointment time, although the next few fixtures could prove crucial.

Chelsea's board have no immediate aims to sack Alonso, but the 44-year-old is under pressure to deliver results in the coming matches, according to new reports.

It has been revealed that the Blues face Nottingham Forest and Crystal Palace next, before a demanding run of fixtures against Liverpool, Manchester City and Aston Villa. The three matches before Christmas could "make or break" Alonso's future at Stamford Bridge.

Chelsea presently sit eighth in the Premier League table, with supporters having already voiced their frustration during the defeat to Leeds.

There are also concerns of a "mutiny" behind the scenes, with it believed that several players are unhappy with Alonso's coaching methods at the training ground and that there is a "terrible atmosphere in the dressing room".

Nevertheless, the hierarchy are understood to believe that injuries have contributed to the team's struggles. Joao Pedro has been absent since the middle of October with a thigh problem, having been an vital figure earlier in the campaign.

The club are hopeful that his return could help spark an improvement in results, although the pressure on Alonso is unlikely to disappear unless performances improve.

Clearlake have made managerial changes a regular feature of their Chelsea project, but dismissing Alonso just months into his tenure would risk repeating a familiar cycle at Stamford Bridge.

The Spaniard is still relatively early into his reign and has had to contend with key absences, particularly Pedro and captain Reece James. Both are usual starters who could make a significant difference to the side, especially in a system that relies on their respective qualities.

The reported dressing-room discontent is concerning, however, and Alonso will need to address that quickly, but it should not automatically mean his position is untenable.

Managers need time to implement their ideas, build relationships and establish consistency. Chelsea have invested in Alonso and should allow him to demonstrate what he can achieve with a fitter squad.

The upcoming fixtures will undoubtedly test that patience, but another change of manager so early in the process would hardly represent a convincing long-term strategy.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Several AC Milan players have been highly praised by the Italian media after the 5-1 dismantling of Frosinone at San Siro.

Milan ended up with goals from five different sources as Goncalo Ramos, Ardon Jashari, Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic all netted, in addition to the opening goal which was an own-goal by Calvani. Adrien Rabiot got three assists, while Diego Moreira shone too.

It was a statement result and a ruthless display of the weapons that the Rossoneri have in transition, and it moves Ruben Amorim’s side back into the top four, while they remain five points off leaders Lazio.

Starting with La Gazzetta dello Sport, they gave the team’s overall performance a score of 8 out of 10, which is the same mark that they gave Amorim for his selections and tactical handling of what could have been a tough game on paper.

Rabiot was the Serie A Man of the Match and he gets the crown from La Gazzetta too, scoring an 8. The worst performer was Davide Bartesaghi, who struggled in his battle with Ghedjemis and got a 5.5.

Moreira matched Rabiot with an 8, while Pulisic and Luka Modric were given a 7.5. Four players scored a 7: Yunus Musah, Ramos, Jashari and Cisse. Sankhoun Diawara (6.5) passed the test, with Koni De Winter, Strahinja Pavlovic and Pervis Estupinan being given a 6.

It has been revealed that corriere dello Sport were a tad harsher with their scoring, giving Rabiot a 7.5 as the highest score. Jashari, Moreira, Modric, Pulisic and Ramos were handed a 7. They gave Cisse a 6.5, and everyone else got a passing score. Amorim (7.5) was also praised.

Sources indicate that tuttosport meanwhile gave Rabiot an 8, distributing 7.5s instead to Moreira, Modric, Pulisic and the coach Amorim. Scores of 7 went to Jashari, Musah, Ramos and Cisse. Gila, De Winter and Diawara got given a 6.5, and everyone else a 6.

#118955. Arsenal: 'Much more complete' - how Madueke has grown and become a key man amid injuries
