Arsenal: 'Much more complete' - how Madueke has grown and become a key man amid injuries

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1280 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Axel Clody | 24 Nov 2026 07:45.
  • Noni Madueke's signing by Arsenal divided opinion before the forward had even stepped onto the pitch.
  • Arriving from Chelsea for £50m, the Englishman joined a squad that already had Bukayo Saka as the owner of the right wing and had to justify an investment in a player who initially seemed destined to be a back-up.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Axel Clody | 24 Nov 2026 07:45.

Noni Madueke's signing by Arsenal divided opinion before the forward had even stepped onto the pitch.

Arriving from Chelsea for £50m, the Englishman joined a squad that already had Bukayo Saka as the owner of the right wing and had to justify an investment in a player who initially seemed destined to be a back-up.

Industry observers note that A little over a year later, the debate is taking on another dimension. With Saka injured, Madueke has been given a longer run of opportunities and has taken the chance. As well as goals and assists, he has contributed in different roles on both sides of the pitch. The 2-2 draw with Newcastle, in which he scored the goal that earned Arsenal a point, was another example of this development.

Sources indicate that mikel Arteta has noticed a change that goes beyond productivity. In a press conference, the manager highlighted the variety that the forward has added to the team's play and his contribution without the ball. And Madueke's growth has followed a concrete path.

In a recent development, madueke has very specific characteristics. Left-footed and explosive, he likes to receive the ball wide on the right, run at the full-back and carry the ball towards the box to shoot or find a team-mate. His short burst of acceleration and ability to change direction make his movements hard to defend when he receives the ball in equal-numbers situations.

That characteristic was already visible at Chelsea. In the 2024-25 season, he was one of the Premier League players who carried the ball into the box the most and created danger mainly through individual runs. The problem was inconsistency in execution: he did not always choose the best moment. Arteta acknowledged the change.

In a recent development, 'He is becoming decisive in games, and that is what we need from our forward players. And he is doing it in several ways, which is something I really like. He has added variety and a lot more connection to his game' - Arteta remarked.

According to recent reports, the numbers help to gauge the growth. According to FotMob's analysis for the 2026-27 Premier League, Madueke creates 3.6 chances per 90 minutes, compared with 1.5 for Saka. It is a significant difference, although it is important to consider that Saka has played fewer minutes.

Recent findings suggest that the improvement also reveals in his ability to contribute without the ball. According to Arteta, Madueke does not always need to receive the ball at his feet to take part in the move.

'And yes, I also love his intensity without the ball. So, I would say he is becoming a much more complete player, and I think he is enjoying it a lot' - Arteta remarked.

In a recent development, the evolution, therefore, is not about abandoning the dribble but about knowing when to use it. Madueke remains a player of individual initiative, only now he seems to understand better how his actions can connect with the collective workings of the team.

The comparison with Saka is inevitable, but the two are not identical players. Both are left-footed and prefer to start from the right to cut inside, but they do so in different ways.

Saka is more refined in decision-making. He has excellent ball control, protects possession under pressure and alternates between carries, short passes and crosses very naturally. His ability to draw two markers and find the free team-mate is also one of Arsenal's main attacking tools.

Madueke, for his part, offers more explosiveness in the first movement and tends to look for the individual duel more often. He is a more vertical player, who likes to accelerate and attack the space left by the full-back. When he is confident, he can disorganise a defence without depending on a long build-up.

The creation data helps illustrate this difference. As well as outperforming Saka in chances created per 90 minutes in FotMob's analysis, Madueke also shows a greater volume of dribbles and progressive carries per minute in another statistical comparison this season. Saka, on the other hand, keeps the advantage in shooting and defensive contribution indicators. They are complementary profiles, not necessarily competitors for a single way of playing.

This difference is valuable for Arteta. Against opponents who defend in a low block, Saka can be more useful to control possession, combine with the midfielders and find the pass that dismantles the marking. Madueke can offer a more direct threat, attacking the full-back and creating situations of individual imbalance.

The Englishman has also shown that he can play on the left, a role he performed when Christos Tzolis was unavailable. There, he needs to adapt his movements: instead of cutting inside with his dominant foot, he can look for the byline and cross with his right. It is not necessarily his ideal position, but the versatility widens Arteta's options and prevents the team from depending on a single alternative for each side.

The competition with Saka, therefore, does not need to be understood as an attempt to take the starter's place. Arsenal need more than one player capable of deciding matches, especially in a long season, with the Premier League, the Champions League and domestic cups. The point is that Madueke is starting to offer arguments to be considered more than a simple replacement.

One detail of this transformation happened away from Arsenal. After being left out of an England squad, Madueke decided to use the international break to train individually. Instead of treating the period as a chance to rest, the forward sought out a specific preparation programme.

Arteta highlighted the player's reaction as an example for the rest of the squad. The manager mentioned that Madueke came back from the break as a different athlete, determined not to accept the situation he was in.

Madueke at Arsenal, season by season.

Premier League 2025-26 vs. 2026-27, per-90 averages.

Sources indicate that premier League games only. Because the seasons have different numbers of minutes, the comparison uses per-90 averages; the total appears below each average. The change compares the averages. Madueke has not yet provided an assist in the Premier League in 2026-27. Data up to 21 November 2026 (matchweek 11).

It has been revealed that 'He went away, decided to train, came back, and he was a different Noni. You could sense that he meant business, and he was not going to accept that situation. Since then, he has been incredible' - Arteta explained, commenting on the player's change of attitude.

In a recent development, the individual work, however, did not start now. In an interview with Sky Sports, Madueke revealed that he has been working for years with specialist coach Saul Isaksson-Hurst, since his time at PSV. The partnership involves technical improvement and individual development, with special attention to the ability to be more decisive in the final third.

It has been revealed that the result has shown up in the numbers: his average of chances created has more than doubled compared with last season, reaching 3.57 per 90 minutes in the Premier League. His dribble success rate has risen from 50% to 55%, while his passing accuracy has gone from 78% to 87%. In open-play crosses, his success rate has jumped from 14% to 33%.

These numbers help explain why Arteta talks about a more complete player. Madueke has not stopped looking for the dribble, but he has started to execute better other actions that previously could limit his influence. The progress has come from different reasons and paths, but the result has arrived and is evident in the current season.

University students are biggest spreaders of COVID

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (721 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Undergraduate students on university campuses played a substantial part in spreading viral variants during the COVID-19 pandemic.Credit: Leonard Ortiz/Digital First Media/Orange County Register/Getty.
  • Universities have become hotbeds of SARS-CoV-2 transmission, according to a massive analysis of more than 85,000 viral genome sequences and other data collected from people with COVID-19.
  • COVID can wake up a slew of dormant viruses inside you.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Undergraduate students on university campuses played a substantial part in spreading viral variants during the COVID-19 pandemic.Credit: Leonard Ortiz/Digital First Media/Orange County Register/Getty.

Universities have become hotbeds of SARS-CoV-2 transmission, according to a massive analysis of more than 85,000 viral genome sequences and other data collected from people with COVID-19.

COVID can wake up a slew of dormant viruses inside you.

COVID can wake up a slew of dormant viruses inside you.

The study, published on 19 November in the journal Cell1, finds that viral transmission between 2021 and 2023 was highest in adolescents aged 15–18 in schools, undergraduates at university and residents in nursing facilities. Undergraduates, in particular, were consistently the first group to start spreading emerging genetic variants of SARS-CoV-2.

Surprisingly, however, staff members at all three types of institution had about the same risk of contracting COVID-19 as did those in their surrounding communities. So, for example, professors were about as likely to get COVID-19 from the coffee baristas in their university towns as they were to get it from a student at their university.

The analysis is among the largest to bring together viral genomic sequences and medical data from people with COVID-19. “The scale is truly impressive,” states Bill Hanage, who studies the evolution of infectious diseases at the Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health in Boston, Massachusetts. “It’s an example of the depth and the detail of the picture that can be painted using the medium of population genomics.”.

It has been revealed that the findings were based on data collected from COVID-19 tests taken by people in Massachusetts between November 2021 and January 2023. The genomic data allowed researchers to trace the path of SARS-CoV-2 variants that emerged over time, and to link this with epidemiological data about the study participants, such as their age and whether they had been vaccinated against COVID-19.

COVID jabs for kids: they’re safe and they work — so why is uptake so patchy?

COVID jabs for kids: they’re safe and they work — so why is uptake so patchy?

According to recent reports, overall, the team found that booster vaccinations helped to reduce SARS-CoV-2 transmission. This was true even for BA.1, an Omicron variant that started to circulate in Massachusetts in late 2021 — a striking result because COVID-19 vaccines at that time hadn’t yet been updated to protect against BA.1, Hanage notes. “That’s an key illustration of how vaccines, even when they’re not perfect, can still be beneficial,” he says.

James Tarkowski: Games Everton defender will miss as red card leaves David Moyes with “major problem”

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (628 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Oliver Thomas | 24 Nov 2026 08:40, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 08:42.
  • James Tarkowski received his first-ever red card in the Premier League as Everton fell to a heavy 4-0 defeat at Brentford on Monday night.
  • The 34-year-old defender had previously been given 74 yellow cards across 350 Premier League appearances but had never been sent off – a top-flight record for the most yellows without ever seeing red.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Oliver Thomas | 24 Nov 2026 08:40, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 08:42.

James Tarkowski received his first-ever red card in the Premier League as Everton fell to a heavy 4-0 defeat at Brentford on Monday night.

The 34-year-old defender had previously been given 74 yellow cards across 350 Premier League appearances but had never been sent off – a top-flight record for the most yellows without ever seeing red.

However, Tarkowski was dismissed in the first half with the Toffees trailing by two goals at the Gtech Community Stadium for a studs-up challenge on the shin of Yehor Yarmolyuk.

Tarkowski had initially thundered into a sliding challenge and won the ball, but his right boot followed through with his studs scraping down the Brentford midfielder’s leg.

On-field referee Craig Pawson gave a yellow card for the challenge, but was then advised by VAR to review the incident at the pitchside monitor, where he ultimately came to the decision to upgrade the yellow to a red.

Tarkowski was deemed to have “committed a challenge that endangers his opponent's safety” with a red card issued for serious foul play.

James Tarkowski is sent off! ? https://t.co/s5ta4f74np.

Tarkowski will therefore serve a three-match suspension and will crucially miss Sunday’s Merseyside derby against rivals Liverpool at the Hill Dickinson Stadium.

The Toffees captain is also banned for a trip to Aston Villa on December 2 and a home clash with Fulham four days later, but he is available to return for an away fixture against Brighton & Hove Albion on December 13.

After taking charge of his record-breaking 593rd game as Everton manager, David Moyes was asked whether the club will look to appeal the red card, and he told Sky Sports: "Don't know yet.

"I thought Tarki got the ball in plenty of time, certainly got there before the player who came in late, but I think Tarki's foot was high, and in that case then there is a chance it can be given.".

In a recent development, speaking to BBC Match of the Day, Moyes added: "My thoughts at the time, I didn't think it was, but when I've looked at it again I think his foot high. Is there enough force for it to be a red card? Not sure about that.".

Sky Sports pundit and former Liverpool defender Jamie Carragher believes that Tarkowski was right to be sent off and feels that Moyes has a “big problem” to deal with ahead of the Merseyside derby.

"It is a red card. It might not have been a red card in 1996, but it is in 2026,” Carragher mentioned on Monday Night Football.

"He knows what he's doing, and he doesn't need to do that. At the last moment, he is trying to pull back on the intensity of the challenge. Don't give [the referee] the option. He doesn't need to do that. I've made tackles like that.".

He added: "David Moyes should be looking at him and thinking [it's 2-0], you've left your mates out there with 10, and it's the Merseyside derby next.

It has been revealed that "For me, it's the biggest game of the season. Everton, biggest game of the season. I hope for the Liverpool players and staff, the biggest game of the season.

"He's brilliant in the box, and that will be a significant problem for Everton. He's so good set-piece-wise.".

Either Jake O'Brien or Michael Keane is expected to play at centre-back alongside Jarrad Branthwaite in the absence of Tarkowski in the next three Premier League games.

A four-goal defeat for Everton has seen them slip to ninth in the Premier League table, with Brentford leapfrogging them into seventh position, albeit sitting just one point above them.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ardon Jashari claims he promised the AC Milan fans he would score, so he was happy to deliver on his promise.

Milan put on a counter-attacking clinic at San Siro on Sunday night against Frosinone, winning 5-1. An own-goal from Gabriele Calvani kicked things off, with Goncalo Ramos, Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic also netting.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

According to recent reports, there was a special moment for Jashari just after coming on at half-time as he scored the third goal of the night and his first for the club. It came in transition, with the Swiss midfielder running in behind and thumping a powerful shot in off the near post, leaving the goalkeeper stunned.

Jashari spoke to SportMediaset after the final whistle at San Siro to reflect on what was a great night both for the team and for him on a personal note, with his words via MilanPress.

How do you feel to have scored and won?

In a recent development, “Finally, I’m very happy with my first goal for Milan. It was a great feeling, and I’m happy for our team. We played a very intense, beautiful game against a tough and united team, both on and off the ball. We won, and we have to continue like this on Thursday, and for the rest of the season.”.

Can we expect the same in Europe now?

According to recent reports, “I hope so. I’m happy with today and I’ll try to continue like this for the team and the fans. It’s very important to have won.”.

Recent findings suggest that ⚽️ GOAL ARDON JASHARI! His first for #ACMilan! 👏 https://t.co/fdfHgOJtfJ.

— SempreMilan (@SempreMilanCom) November 22, 2026.

What can you tell us about your position today?

“I played next to Luka today. Normally, strikers score goals, but today it was my turn. When I score, I score beautiful goals (smiles). It seemed like the goal against Venezia, but today it was even better because it was mine. The celebration was the same. I promised the fans I would score, and that’s what happened.”.

“In my opinion, it’s very key to continue like this. The season is too long until May. Now it’s November. We’ve had a good season so far, but there are five months to go until May. We need these results against all our opponents. Today it was Frosinone, there’s still a lot to do.

Recent findings suggest that “When you play for Milan, you have to win games and trophies, but it’s November. Everyone knows what it means to wear the Milan shirt, it’s important to continue like this. When you win, you’re good, when you lose, you’re not. It doesn’t matter who scores.”.

Industry News: Barcelona transfer news: Catalan giants could receive £10m windfall from PSG transfer

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (378 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Axel Clody | 24 Nov 2026 08:45.
  • Paris Saint-Germain could indirectly do Barcelona a favour in the January transfer window.
  • According to AS, Antonio Nusa is among the capital club's preferred targets, alongside Abde Ezzalzouli, Gianluca Prestianni, Ibrahim Maza, Luis Diaz and Estevao.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Axel Clody | 24 Nov 2026 08:45.

Paris Saint-Germain could indirectly do Barcelona a favour in the January transfer window. In search of a potential attacking reinforcement after the long-term injuries to Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue, the capital club have drawn up an initial shortlist.

According to AS, Antonio Nusa is among the capital club's preferred targets, alongside Abde Ezzalzouli, Gianluca Prestianni, Ibrahim Maza, Luis Diaz and Estevao. These players will be difficult to sign in the January transfer window. Paris have already experienced that, having been rebuffed over Estevao, while Prestianni wants to finish the season at Benfica.

It has been revealed that in that sense, Abde Ezzalzouli could be an interesting option. 3Cat confirms that the Morocco international is among the targets being studied by PSG to strengthen their attack in January. Aged 24, Abde is enjoying a good start to the season, with four goals and one assist in 13 games for the Andalusian club.

His profile has reportedly caught the attention of the Parisian hierarchy, especially as the player now shares the same agent as Achraf Hakimi.

This could ease discussions. The rumour is also being followed closely in Barcelona, as a potential transfer of the Real Betis winger would allow Barcelona to recoup a significant sum.

The Catalan outlet recalls that in September 2023, Barcelona sold Abde to Real Betis for £6.4m (€7.5m). In that deal, they kept a share of the Moroccan's economic rights. Initially set at 50%, it was later reduced to 20% in February 2025 as part of the agreement concerning Vitor Roque.

A £51m (€60m) transfer, the amount of Abde's release clause, would therefore bring Barcelona £10m. PSG would have the opportunity to sign a promising 24-year-old winger for a reasonable amount, while doing their Spanish rivals a serious financial favour by triggering the clause.

Industry observers note that this sum could give the Barcelona hierarchy more room for manoeuvre to strengthen Hansi Flick's squad this winter. The German boss is notably looking to sign a centre-back.

In a recent development, it should be noted that, at this stage, no agreement or advanced negotiation has been declared for Abde's arrival at PSG. It remains to be seen whether Paris will actually take action.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AC Milan produced their best attacking display of the season on Sunday night as they put five goals past Frosinone at San Siro.

An own-goal from Gabriele Calvani early on set the tone, with Goncalo Ramos, Ardon Jashari, Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic all netting in the rout. The ruthless counter-attacking display moves Milan back inside the top four, after wins from Como, Roma and Lazio earlier in the round.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

According to recent reports, the match stats make for interesting reading. Milan edged possession with 54%, generating 2.50 Expected Goals – so scoring double what they created – but also having five major chances which matches the number of goals scored.

Frosinone remarkably had more shots in total (15 to 12), but they were more wasteful with only three on target to the Rossoneri’s eight. The visitors also racked up nine corners, the most Milan have conceded all season.

Industry observers note that 📊 The stats from the win against Frosinone. pic.twitter.com/ERVTj98m9Y.

— MilanData📊 (@acmilandata) November 22, 2026.

Only Nereo Rocco’s (29) and Lajos Czeizler’s (31) Milan sides scored more goals than Ruben Amorim’s (28) in their first 12 matches in charge in Serie A.

Adrien Rabiot is the first Milan midfielder to be involved in at least one goal (including goals and assists) in seven consecutive Serie A appearances since Kaká in 2004, and he became the first midfielder in the last 20 years of Serie A with more than 10 goals in his first 10 games in a single season.

With his sixth goal in his 10th Serie A appearance for Milan at 20 years and 31 days, Alphadjo Cisse became the second-youngest Rossoneri player to reach this milestone in his first 10 appearances in the three-points-for-a-win era, after Alexandre Pato , who achieved it at 18 years and 189 days.

No team has scored more goals than Milan in the first 15 minutes of play in the five major European leagues right now underway (7, like Barcelona and Chelsea).

Milan are now unbeaten in all seven meetings against Frosinone in Serie A (W5 D2): among the teams against which they have never lost in the competition, the Rossoneri have played more games only against Pisa (14 – six also against Crotone and Lecco).

It has been revealed that milan have won five of their last six league games (L1), scoring at least two goals in each, after failing to win three of their previous four (D3). The last time they scored more than one goal in a run of Serie A matches was between September 2020 and January 2021, when they managed 15 games.

This season’s Premier League title race may be locked in a paralysed state of uncertainty but Arsenal, the defending champions, are determined to keep it interesting.

City’s lead at the top is back to three points but Arsenal’s win here was unlikely to have sent any shivers down the spines of Enzo Maresca and his players in this phoney mess of a season.

It was not until the 80th minute that Arsenal finally registered their first shot on target, and that was the moment which ended their cycle of frustration at the City Ground.

Just when it appeared Mikel Arteta was heading for a third successive goalless draw at the home of Nottingham Forest, substitute Noni Madueke’s deflected strike proved the difference.

🟡 𝗧𝗘𝗔𝗠𝙉𝙀𝙒𝙎 🔵 Your Sunday starters 👊 🤝 Presented by @deel.

Fascinating stuff from Sam Dean this morning, who has profiled a member of Mikel Arteta’s inner circle who is not listed on Arsenal’s website. Germán Castaños, an expert in innovation who has written multiple books on alternative thinking, has become a key member of the team. Things started with a phone call with Nicolas Jover, then a meeting with Arteta and now he splits his time between Argentina and London. Find out more about Arsenal’s mystery man and his methods here.

In the ordinary course of a Premier League season, you would say Manchester City have applied pressure on Arsenal by opening up a six-point lead before the champions play at Nottingham Forest this afternoon.

This is not a normal Premier League season though, and we await to discover if the top of the league table is simply a mirage.

Regardless, Mikel Arteta and his Arsenal players have their own motivations to accumulate as many points as possible before January as they seek to retain the title for the first time since the 1930s.

Arsenal have struggled at the City Ground, drawing 0-0 on their last two Premier League visits. They also lost at Forest in May 2023, a result which confirmed Manchester City as champions at Arsenal’s expense, and were knocked out of the FA Cup by Forest in January 2022.

Forest are yet to score a home league goal under Oliver Glasner, another data point suggesting this will be a low-scoring game.

That might not be the full story though, with Forest creating a hatful of chances in their defeat at Crystal Palace last week and Arsenal also playing a more inventive, technical game with the ball so far this season.

Arsenal have yet to score from a non-penalty set-piece, and their percentage of goals from open play is now the highest in the Premier League.

It has been revealed that morgan Gibbs-White is a doubt after sustaining what Glasner described as a “minor muscle injury” at Palace and his involvement in the game will be a last-minute call. With the exception of Christos Tzolis, Piero Hincapie and long-term absentee William Saliba, Arsenal’s squad is in pretty good health. Bukayo Saka, Martin Odegaard, Kai Havertz, Riccardo Calafiori and Ben White could be recalled to Arteta’s starting XI after starting the Champions League win over Lille on the bench.

Full team news on the way shortly.

Kevin De Bruyne responds to Man City "disgrace" claims after Premier League guilty verdict

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Oliver Thomas | 24 Nov 2026 09:01, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 10:51.

Kevin De Bruyne has made his feelings for Manchester City crystal clear as he has spoken out for the first time since the club were found guilty of breaching Premier League financial regulations.

At the end of September, an independent commission found Man City guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of the Premier League’s financial rules and the majority of charges in relation to its failure to co-operate with the investigation.

The Citizens are accused of using "sham" contracts with a number of commercial partners to disguise secret funding of more than £830m and artificially inflate revenues between the 2009-10 and 2017-18 seasons.

Man City continue to plead their innocence and lodged an appeal last month, stating that “a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence exists in support of all of its positions, relating to this case.”.

A plethora of possible sanctions have been mooted should Man City’s guilty verdict be upheld, including heavy fines, transfer bans, stripping titles, points deductions leading to relegation and expulsion from the Premier League.

De Bruyne spent 10 glorious years at the Etihad Stadium before leaving in the summer of 2025 and will go down as one of Man City’s greatest-ever players after playing a crucial role in the club winning 19 trophies during his time at the club.

The Belgian playmaker won six Premier League titles, five EFL Cups and three FA Cups, while he also won the Champions League during a historic treble-winning season in 2022-23.

The two-time Premier League Player of the Season scored 108 goals and provided 177 assists in 422 appearances for Man City across all competitions, with 119 of those assists recorded in the Premier League to rank him second on the all-time list behind Ryan Giggs (162).

De Bruyne has made a welcome retuned to Manchester as his current club Napoli prepare to face City in the Champions League on Tuesday night.

While De Bruyne has acknowledged that some people may have different opinions over Man City’s guilty verdict, the legendary midfielder himself has insisted that his feelings towards the club will “never change”.

"My feeling's never been different,” he told reporters at a press conference. “Honestly, the way that I feel is just the way that I've been treated by this club, what I've done with this club for me personally, and how we've worked together as a group. Of course, it's a lot of things that's been going on but I cannot change anything about that.

"I'm proud of what I've done as a football player, and honestly... This is my club! I love the owners, I've talked about a lot of stuff outside of football, I've even spoken to Khaldoon [Al Mubarak] how to buy a club and everything, so there's a lot of things that goes around after this.

"I've nothing but affection for this club and that will never change! Even now, the people who treated me for 10 years exceptionally, my family and everything, that's for me the most vital and for me, that is it to be honest.".

Intense criticism has been aimed at Man City since the guilty verdict, but De Bruyne cannot "change anything" about people calling his former club a "disgrace" and still believes that everything he personally achieved with the club was won fairly.

“It [the verdict] still doesn’t change, my football has not changed,” De Bruyne said. “In life there are rules, but everybody plays on the limit.

Industry observers note that “I played in between the white lines, I competed with other players and I had many experiences with my teams, with the players. That’s the thing I value most.

“In my career, the most important thing is the relationships between everybody that I had and how you manage these things.

Recent findings suggest that “I’ve given my all and that’s not going to change in my mind. I don’t think a lot of ­people will change in their mind how they view me as a player or how we played. Other people may be disgraced a bit, but I can’t change anything about that.”.

Tuesday’s contest will mark De Bruyne’s second appearance back at the Etihad since departing Man City, and the 35-year-old will be hoping for a much smoother evening this time around.

On his previous visit last year, a first-half red card forced ex-Napoli boss Antonio Conte to reshuffle his side, with De Bruyne the unfortunate player to be sacrificed early in a 2-0 defeat.
